sentences.zh: 太祖初起，草創闊略，宮闈未有位號，但循國俗稱「福晉」。

translations.literal: When Taizu first rose, founding was broad and rough; the inner palace had no ranks or titles, and they only followed national custom in calling them "fujin."
translations.idiomatic: In Taizu’s early rise, institutions were still broadly sketched; the inner palace had no formal ranks and consorts were known only by the national custom as fujin.

sentences.zh: 福晉蓋「可敦」之轉音，史述后妃，後人緣飾名之，非當時本稱也。

translations.literal: Fujin is roughly a transliteration of "khatun"; when histories describe empresses and consorts, later men embellished the names—this was not the original title of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Fujin is essentially a transliteration of khatun; when later historians speak of empresses and consorts they adorn the record with titles that were not the names actually used at the time.

sentences.zh: 崇德改元，五宮並建，位號既明，等威漸辨。

translations.literal: When the Chongde reign era was adopted, the five palaces were all established; ranks and titles were now clear, and precedence gradually distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: With the adoption of the Chongde reign title, five palaces were established at once; titles were fixed and ranks of precedence gradually took shape.

sentences.zh: 世祖定鼎，循前代舊典，

translations.literal: When Shizu fixed the capital, he followed the old statutes of former dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: After Shizu established the dynasty at Beijing, he followed the precedents of earlier ages.

sentences.zh: 順治十五年，採禮官之議：乾清宮設夫人一，淑儀一，婉侍六，柔婉、芳婉皆三十；

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Shunzhi, he adopted the proposals of the ritual officials: in the Palace of Heavenly Purity there were to be one lady, one shuyi, six wanshi, and thirty each of rouwan and fangwan;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Shunzhi, he took up the ritual officials’ proposals: the Palace of Heavenly Purity was to have one lady, one shuyi, six wanshi, and thirty each of rouwan and fangwan;

sentences.zh: 慈寧宮設貞容一、慎容二，勤侍無定數；

translations.literal: the Palace of Compassionate Tranquility was to have one zhenrong and two shenrong, with no fixed number of qinshi;
translations.idiomatic: the Palace of Compassionate Tranquility one zhenrong and two shenrong, with no fixed quota of qinshi;

sentences.zh: 又置女官。

translations.literal: female palace officers were also to be appointed.
translations.idiomatic: and female palace officers were also to be appointed.

sentences.zh: 循明六局一司之制，議定而未行。

translations.literal: Following the Ming system of six bureaus and one office, the plan was settled but never carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Following the Ming model of six bureaus and one office, the scheme was agreed upon but never put into practice.

sentences.zh: 康熙以後，典制大備。

translations.literal: After the Kangxi reign, the canonical regulations were fully complete.
translations.idiomatic: From the Kangxi reign onward, the palace regulations were brought to full maturity.

sentences.zh: 皇后居中宮；

translations.literal: The empress dwelt in the central palace;
translations.idiomatic: The empress occupied the central palace;

sentences.zh: 皇貴妃一，貴妃二，妃四，嬪六，貴人、常在、答應無定數，分居東、西十二宮。

translations.literal: there was one imperial noble consort, two imperial consorts, four consorts, six ladies, and an unfixed number of noble ladies, attendants, and responders, each quartered in the twelve palaces of the east and west.
translations.idiomatic: there was one imperial noble consort, two imperial consorts, four consorts, six ladies, and an open number of noble ladies, attendants, and responders, quartered across the twelve eastern and western palaces.

sentences.zh: 東六宮：曰景仁，曰承乾，曰鍾粹，曰延禧，曰永和，曰景陽；

translations.literal: The six eastern palaces were called Jingren, Chengqian, Zhongcui, Yanxi, Yonghe, and Jingyang;
translations.idiomatic: The six eastern palaces were Jingren, Chengqian, Zhongcui, Yanxi, Yonghe, and Jingyang;

sentences.zh: 西六宮：曰永壽，曰翊坤，曰儲秀，曰啟祥，曰長春，曰咸福。

translations.literal: the six western palaces were called Yongshou, Yikun, Chuxiu, Qixiang, Changchun, and Xianfu.
translations.idiomatic: the six western palaces Yongshou, Yikun, Chuxiu, Qixiang, Changchun, and Xianfu.

sentences.zh: 諸宮皆有宮女子供使令。

translations.literal: Every palace had palace women to carry out orders.
translations.idiomatic: Each palace had palace women assigned to service.

sentences.zh: 每三歲選八旗秀女，戶部主之；

translations.literal: Every three years maidens of the Eight Banners were selected, under the Board of Revenue;
translations.idiomatic: Every three years maidens were chosen from the Eight Banners under the Board of Revenue;

sentences.zh: 每歲選內務府屬旗秀女，內務府主之。

translations.literal: each year maidens of the banners subordinate to the Imperial Household Department were selected, under that department.
translations.idiomatic: and each year maidens from the banners under the Imperial Household Department were chosen by that office.

sentences.zh: 秀女入宮，妃、嬪、貴人惟上命。

translations.literal: When maidens entered the palace, appointment as consort, lady, or noble lady depended solely on the sovereign’s command.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside the palace, promotion to consort, lady, or noble lady rested solely on the emperor’s order.

sentences.zh: 選宮女子，貴人以上，得選世家女；

translations.literal: In choosing palace women, for ranks of noble lady and above, daughters of eminent families might be chosen;
translations.idiomatic: For palace women of noble lady rank and above, daughters of distinguished families could be selected;

sentences.zh: 貴人以下，但選拜唐阿以下女。

translations.literal: below noble lady, only daughters of bondsmen and below were chosen.
translations.idiomatic: below that rank only daughters of bondsmen and lower status were taken.

sentences.zh: 宮女子侍上，自常在、答應漸進至妃、嬪，后妃諸姑、姊妹不赴選。

translations.literal: Palace women who attended the sovereign might advance from attendant or responder step by step to consort or lady; the aunts and sisters of empresses and consorts did not enter selection.
translations.idiomatic: Palace women who served the emperor might rise from attendant or responder to lady or consort; the aunts and sisters of empresses and consorts were excluded from selection.

sentences.zh: 帝祖母曰「太皇太后」，母曰「皇太后」，居慈寧、壽康、寧壽諸宮。

translations.literal: The emperor’s grandmother was called "grand empress dowager," his mother "empress dowager," and they dwelt in the palaces of Compassionate Tranquility, Longevity and Health, and Tranquil Longevity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor’s grandmother was styled Grand Empress Dowager and his mother Empress Dowager; they lived in the palaces of Compassionate Tranquility, Longevity and Health, and Tranquil Longevity.

sentences.zh: 先朝妃、嬪稱太妃、太嬪，隨皇太后同居，與嗣皇帝，年皆逾五十，乃始得相見。

translations.literal: Consorts and ladies of the previous reign were called grand consort and grand lady; they lived with the empress dowager, and only when both they and the succeeding emperor were past fifty might they meet.
translations.idiomatic: Consorts and ladies of the previous reign were styled Grand Consort and Grand Lady and lived with the empress dowager; they might meet the new emperor only when both parties were over fifty.

sentences.zh: 諸宮殿設太監，秩最高不逾四品，員額有定數，廩給有定量，分領執事有定程。

translations.literal: Every palace had eunuchs appointed; the highest rank did not exceed the fourth grade, quotas were fixed, rations set, and duties divided with fixed schedules.
translations.idiomatic: Each palace had eunuchs whose highest rank did not exceed the fourth grade; numbers, stipends, and duties were all fixed by regulation.

sentences.zh: 此其大較也。

translations.literal: This is the general outline.
translations.idiomatic: Such, in broad outline, was the system.

sentences.zh: 二百數十年，壺化肅雍，詖謁蓋寡，內鮮燕溺匹嫡之嫌，外絕權戚蠹國之釁，彬彬盛矣。

translations.literal: For more than two hundred years, the inner realm was governed with solemn harmony; private petitions were few; within, there was little of the suspicion that comes from favoritism and usurpation of the legitimate wife’s place; without, the malady of powerful kin ruining the state was cut off—civil order flourished abundantly.
translations.idiomatic: For more than two centuries the inner court was governed with grave harmony, private petitions were rare, within the palace there was scarcely the jealousy of rival consorts, and without there was no plague of powerful kin corrupting the state—a civil order of rare fullness.

sentences.zh: 追尊四代，惟宣皇后著氏族，且有繼室，託始於是。

translations.literal: In posthumous honor of four generations, only Empress Xuan records her clan name, and there was also a succession consort—the account begins here.
translations.idiomatic: Of the four generations raised to posthumous honor, only Empress Xuan is recorded with her clan name and with a succession consort; the narrative begins with her.

sentences.zh: 歷朝居正號者，謹而次之，並及妃、嬪有子若受後朝尊封者。

translations.literal: Those of each reign who held the principal title are set forth carefully in order, together with consorts and ladies who bore sons or received honored titles from a later reign.
translations.idiomatic: For each reign those who held the principal title are treated in due order, together with consorts and ladies who bore sons or were honored by a later dynasty.

sentences.zh: 世祖以漢女為妃，高宗以回女為妃，附書之，以其僅見也。

translations.literal: Shizu took a Han woman as consort, and Gaozong took a Hui woman as consort; these are appended because such cases are rarely seen.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu’s marriage to a Han consort and Gaozong’s to a Hui consort are noted separately, as such cases are uncommon.

sentences.zh: 顯祖宣皇后，喜塔臘氏，都督阿古女。

translations.literal: Empress Xuan of Xianzu, of the Xitala clan, was the daughter of Commander Agu.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xuan of Xianzu, of the Xitala clan, was the daughter of Commander Agu.

sentences.zh: 歸顯祖為嫡妃。

translations.literal: She was married to Xianzu as his principal consort.
translations.idiomatic: She became Xianzu’s principal consort.

sentences.zh: 歲己未，太祖生。

translations.literal: In the year jiwei, Taizu was born.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiwei year Taizu was born.

sentences.zh: 歲己巳，崩，

translations.literal: In the year jisi, she died.
translations.idiomatic: In the jisi year she died.

sentences.zh: 順治五年，與肇祖原皇后、興祖直皇后、景祖翼皇后同時追諡。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shunzhi, at the same time posthumous titles were conferred on her together with the Original Empress of the Founding Ancestor, the Upright Empress of the Rising Ancestor, and the Wing Empress of the Illustrious Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Shunzhi, she was given a posthumous title at the same time as the Original Empress of the Founding Ancestor, the Upright Empress of the Rising Ancestor, and the Wing Empress of the Illustrious Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 子三：太祖、舒爾哈齊、雅爾哈齊。

translations.literal: Sons, three: Taizu, Šurhaci, and Yarhači.
translations.idiomatic: She bore three sons: Taizu, Šurhaci, and Yarhači.

sentences.zh: 女一，下嫁噶哈善哈斯虎。

translations.literal: Daughters, one, who married downward to Gahasan Hasihu.
translations.idiomatic: She had one daughter, who married Gahasan Hasihu.

sentences.zh: 繼妃，納喇氏，哈達部長萬所撫族女。

translations.literal: The succession consort, of the Nara clan, was a kinswoman raised by Wan, chief of the Hada.
translations.idiomatic: The succession consort, of the Nara clan, was a kinswoman whom Wan, chief of Hada, had raised.

sentences.zh: 遇太祖寡恩，年十九，俾分居，予產獨薄。

translations.literal: She met with Taizu’s scant favor; at nineteen she was made to live apart, and her allotment of property alone was meager.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu showed her little favor; at nineteen she was set up in a separate household and given a share of property smaller than the rest.

sentences.zh: 子一，巴雅喇。

translations.literal: Sons, one: Bayara.
translations.idiomatic: She bore one son, Bayara.

sentences.zh: 庶妃，李佳氏。

translations.literal: A secondary consort, the Li clan, Jia.
translations.idiomatic: Secondary consort Li of the Jia lineage.

sentences.zh: 子一，穆爾哈齊。

translations.literal: Sons, one: Murhaci.
translations.idiomatic: She bore one son, Murhaci.

sentences.zh: 太祖孝慈高皇后，納喇氏，葉赫部長楊吉砮女。

translations.literal: Empress Xiaoci the High of Taizu, of the Nara clan, was the daughter of Yangginu, chief of the Yehe.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu’s Empress Xiaoci the High, of the Nara clan, was the daughter of Yangginu, chief of Yehe.

sentences.zh: 太祖初起兵，如葉赫，楊吉砮以后許焉。

translations.literal: When Taizu first raised his army and went to Yehe, Yangginu betrothed the empress to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu first took up arms and went to Yehe, Yangginu promised him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 楊吉砮為明總兵李成梁所殺，子納林布祿繼為貝勒，又為成梁擊破。

translations.literal: Yangginu was killed by the Ming regional commander Li Chengliang; his son Narimbulu succeeded as beile and was again defeated by Chengliang.
translations.idiomatic: Yangginu was killed by the Ming commander Li Chengliang; his son Narimbulu became beile and was in turn defeated by Chengliang.

sentences.zh: 歲戊子秋九月，以后來歸，上率諸貝勒、大臣迎之，大宴成禮。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn in the year wuzi, the empress came in marriage; the sovereign led the beiles and ministers to welcome her, and a great feast completed the rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the wuzi year she arrived as bride; the sovereign led the beiles and ministers to receive her, and a great feast completed the wedding rites.

sentences.zh: 是歲，后年十四。

translations.literal: That year the empress was fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: She was fourteen that year.

sentences.zh: 歲壬辰冬十月，太宗生。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter in the year renchen, Taizong was born.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the renchen year Taizong was born.

sentences.zh: 歲癸卯秋，后病作，思見母，上遣使迎焉，納林布祿不許。

translations.literal: In autumn of the year guimao the empress fell ill, longing to see her mother; the sovereign sent envoys to bring her, but Narimbulu would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the guimao year she fell ill and longed to see her mother; the sovereign sent envoys to fetch her, but Narimbulu refused.

sentences.zh: 九月庚辰，后崩，年二十九。

translations.literal: On gengchen, the ninth month, the empress died, aged twenty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen in the ninth month she died, aged twenty-nine.

sentences.zh: 后莊敬聰慧，詞氣婉順，得譽不喜，聞惡言，愉悅不改其常。

translations.literal: The empress was grave, respectful, intelligent, and clever; her words were gentle and compliant; she took no joy in praise, and when she heard harsh words she remained pleased and did not change her usual manner.
translations.idiomatic: She was dignified, intelligent, and quick-witted, gentle in speech and bearing; praise did not delight her, and harsh words did not alter her even temper.

sentences.zh: 不好諂諛，不信讒佞，耳無妄聽，口無妄言。

translations.literal: She did not favor flattery, did not trust slanderers; her ears heard nothing rashly, her mouth spoke nothing rashly.
translations.idiomatic: She disliked flattery, put no faith in slander, and neither listened nor spoke without due cause.

sentences.zh: 不預外事，殫誠畢慮以事上。

translations.literal: She did not meddle in outside affairs, but devoted her whole sincerity and thought to serving the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: She did not meddle in public affairs but gave her whole heart and mind to serving the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 及崩，上深悼之，喪斂祭享有加禮，不飲酒茹葷者逾月。

translations.literal: When she died, the sovereign mourned her deeply; burial, encoffining, and sacrifices were performed with added ceremony, and for more than a month he drank no wine and ate no meat.
translations.idiomatic: At her death the sovereign grieved deeply; her funeral rites were performed with exceptional honor, and for more than a month he abstained from wine and meat.

sentences.zh: 越三載，葬赫圖阿拉尼雅滿山岡，

translations.literal: After three years she was buried on the hillock of Niyaman at Hetu Ala.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later she was buried on Niyaman Hill at Hetu Ala.

sentences.zh: 遷葬東京楊魯山，

translations.literal: Her tomb was moved to Mount Yanglu in Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Her remains were later moved to Mount Yanglu in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 再遷葬瀋陽石嘴頭山，是為福陵，

translations.literal: Again her tomb was moved to Shizuitou Hill in Shenyang—this is the Fuling mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: And again to Shizuitou Hill in Shenyang, which became the Fuling mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 上諡孝慈昭憲純德真順承天育聖武皇后，

translations.literal: She was given the posthumous title Empress Xiaoci Zhaoxian Chunde Zhenshun Chengtian Yusheng Wu.
translations.idiomatic: She received the posthumous title Empress Xiaoci Zhaoxian Chunde Zhenshun Chengtian Yusheng Wu.

sentences.zh: 祔太廟，

translations.literal: Her tablet was placed in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Her spirit tablet was enshrined in the Grand Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 改諡。

translations.literal: Her posthumous title was later changed.
translations.idiomatic: Her posthumous title was later revised.

sentences.zh: 雍正、乾隆累加諡，曰孝慈昭憲敬順仁徽懿德慶顯承天輔聖高皇后。

translations.literal: Under Yongzheng and Qianlong additional honorifics were repeatedly added, so that she was called Empress Xiaoci Zhaoxian Jingshun Renhui Yide Qingxian Chengtian Fusheng Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzheng and Qianlong added further honorifics until she was styled Empress Xiaoci Zhaoxian Jingshun Renhui Yide Qingxian Chengtian Fusheng Gao.

sentences.zh: 子一，太宗。

translations.literal: Sons, one: Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: She bore one son, Taizong.

sentences.zh: 元妃，佟佳氏。

translations.literal: The primary consort, of the Tunggiya clan.
translations.idiomatic: Primary consort, of the Tunggiya clan.

sentences.zh: 歸太祖最早。

translations.literal: She was married to Taizu earliest of all.
translations.idiomatic: She was Taizu’s earliest consort.

sentences.zh: 子二：褚英、代善。

translations.literal: Sons, two: Cuyen and Daišan.
translations.idiomatic: She bore two sons, Cuyen and Daišan.

sentences.zh: 女一，下嫁何和禮。

translations.literal: Daughters, one, who married downward to Hohori.
translations.idiomatic: She had one daughter, who married Hohori.

sentences.zh: 繼妃，富察氏。

translations.literal: The succession consort, of the Fuca clan.
translations.idiomatic: Succession consort, of the Fuca clan.

sentences.zh: 歸太祖亦在孝慈皇后前。

translations.literal: Her marriage to Taizu also preceded that of Empress Xiaoci.
translations.idiomatic: She had joined Taizu even before Empress Xiaoci.

sentences.zh: 歲癸巳，葉赫諸部來侵，上夜駐軍，寢甚酣，妃呼上覺曰：「爾方寸亂耶，懼耶？

translations.literal: In the year guisi the Yehe tribes came to attack; the sovereign encamped by night and slept very soundly. The consort roused him and said, "Is your mind in disorder, or are you afraid?
translations.idiomatic: In the guisi year the Yehe tribes attacked; the sovereign camped for the night and slept deeply. The consort woke him and said, "Is your mind troubled, or are you afraid?

sentences.zh: 九國兵來攻，豈酣寢時耶？」

translations.literal: The armies of nine states are coming to attack—can this be a time for sound sleep?"
translations.idiomatic: Nine states’ armies are upon us—is this a time to sleep so soundly?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「我果懼，安能酣寢？

translations.literal: The sovereign said, "If I were truly afraid, how could I sleep so soundly?
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "If I were afraid, how could I sleep so soundly?

sentences.zh: 我聞葉赫來侵，以其無期，時以為念。

translations.literal: When I heard that Yehe would invade, because the time was uncertain I kept it in mind.
translations.idiomatic: When I heard Yehe would attack, not knowing when, I kept it constantly in mind.

sentences.zh: 既至，我心安矣。

translations.literal: Now that they have come, my heart is at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Now that they have come, my mind is at rest.

sentences.zh: 我若負葉赫，天必厭之，安得不懼？

translations.literal: If I had wronged Yehe, Heaven would surely detest me—how could I not fear?
translations.idiomatic: If I had wronged Yehe, Heaven would surely reject me—how could I not fear?

sentences.zh: 今我順天命，安疆土，彼糾九國以虐無咎之人，天不佑也！」

translations.literal: Now I follow Heaven’s mandate and secure the borders; they have rallied nine states to abuse the guiltless—Heaven will not aid them!"
translations.idiomatic: Now I follow Heaven’s mandate and secure the realm; they have rallied nine states to harm the innocent—Heaven will not help them!"

sentences.zh: 安寢如故。

translations.literal: He slept at ease as before.
translations.idiomatic: And he slept on as before.

sentences.zh: 及旦，遂破敵。

translations.literal: At dawn he defeated the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 天命五年，妃得罪，死。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianming the consort was found guilty and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianming she was found guilty and put to death.

sentences.zh: 子二：莽古爾泰、德格類。

translations.literal: Sons, two: Manggūltai and Degelei.
translations.idiomatic: She bore two sons, Manggūltai and Degelei.

sentences.zh: 女一，名莽古濟，下嫁鎖諾木杜稜。

translations.literal: Daughters, one, named Mangguji, who married downward to Suonuomu Dulei.
translations.idiomatic: She had one daughter, named Mangguji, who married Suonuomu Dulei.

sentences.zh: 大妃，納喇氏，烏喇貝勒滿泰女。

translations.literal: The grand consort, of the Nara clan, was the daughter of Mantai, beile of Ula.
translations.idiomatic: Grand consort, of the Nara clan, was the daughter of Mantai, beile of Ula.

sentences.zh: 歲辛丑，歸太祖，年十二。

translations.literal: In the year xinchou she came in marriage to Taizu, aged twelve.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinchou year she joined Taizu as his consort, aged twelve.

sentences.zh: 孝慈皇后崩，立為大妃。

translations.literal: When Empress Xiaoci died, she was established as grand consort.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Xiaoci died, she was made grand consort.

sentences.zh: 天命十一年七月，太祖有疾，浴於湯泉。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Tianming, in the seventh month Taizu fell ill and bathed at the hot springs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Tianming, in the seventh month Taizu fell ill and went to bathe at the hot springs.

sentences.zh: 八月，疾大漸，乘舟自太子河還，召大妃出迎，入渾河。

translations.literal: In the eighth month his illness grew grave; he took a boat back from the Taizi River, summoned the grand consort to come out and welcome him, and entered the Hun River.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month his illness worsened; he returned by boat along the Taizi River, summoned the grand consort to meet him, and entered the Hun River.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，舟次靉鷄堡，上崩。

translations.literal: On gengxu the boat halted at Aigibao Fort and the sovereign died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu the boat stopped at Aigibao Fort, and the sovereign died.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，大妃殉焉，年三十七。

translations.literal: On xinhai the grand consort followed him in death, aged thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai the grand consort followed him in death; she was thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 同殉者，二庶妃。

translations.literal: Those who followed in death with her were two secondary consorts.
translations.idiomatic: Two secondary consorts died with her.

sentences.zh: 妃子三：阿濟格、多爾袞、多鐸。

translations.literal: Consort's sons, three: Ajige, Dorgon, and Dodo.
translations.idiomatic: She bore three sons: Ajige, Dorgon, and Dodo.

sentences.zh: 順治初，多爾袞攝政，七年，上諡孝烈恭敏獻哲仁和贊天儷聖武皇后，祔太廟。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi, Dorgon served as regent; in the seventh year the sovereign conferred the posthumous title Empress Xiaolie Gongmin Xianzhe Renhe Zantian Lishèng Wu, and her tablet was placed in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi, while Dorgon was regent, in the seventh year the emperor posthumously titled her Empress Xiaolie Gongmin Xianzhe Renhe Zantian Lishèng Wu and enshrined her in the Grand Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 八年，多爾袞得罪，罷諡，出廟。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Dorgon was found guilty; her posthumous title was revoked and her tablet was removed from the temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, after Dorgon fell from grace, her posthumous title was stripped and her tablet was removed from the temple.

sentences.zh: 壽康太妃，博爾濟吉特氏，科爾沁郡王孔果爾女。

translations.literal: The Shoukang grand imperial consort, of the Borjigit clan, was the daughter of Kongguor, prince of the commandery of Khorchin.
translations.idiomatic: The Shoukang grand imperial consort, of the Borjigit clan, was the daughter of Kongguor, prince of the commandery of Khorchin.

sentences.zh: 太祖諸妃中最老壽，

translations.literal: Among all of Taizu's consorts she lived the longest.
translations.idiomatic: Of all Taizu's consorts she lived the longest.

sentences.zh: 聖祖即位，尊為皇曾祖壽康太妃，

translations.literal: When Shengzu ascended the throne, she was honored as Imperial Great-Great-Grandmother Shoukang Grand Imperial Consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Shengzu came to the throne, she was honored as Imperial Great-Great-Grandmother Shoukang Grand Imperial Consort.

sentences.zh: 薨。

translations.literal: She died.
translations.idiomatic: She died.

sentences.zh: 太祖諸妃稱側妃者四：*伊爾根覺羅氏，子一，阿巴泰，女一，下嫁達爾漢；

translations.literal: Four of Taizu's consorts were called side consorts: *the Yirgen Gioro clan, one son Abatai, one daughter who married downward to Darhan;
translations.idiomatic: Four of Taizu's consorts were styled side consorts: the Yirgen Gioro clan, one son, Abatai, and one daughter who married Darhan;

sentences.zh: *納喇氏，孝慈皇后女弟，女一，下嫁固爾布什；

translations.literal: *the Nara clan, younger sister of Empress Xiaoci, one daughter who married downward to Gurbushi;
translations.idiomatic: The Nara clan, Empress Xiaoci's younger sister, one daughter who married Gurbushi;

sentences.zh: *其二皆無出。

translations.literal: *the other two both had no issue.
translations.idiomatic: The other two bore no children.

sentences.zh: 稱庶妃者五：*兆佳氏，子一，阿拜；

translations.literal: Five were called secondary consorts: *the Joogiya clan, one son Abai;
translations.idiomatic: Five were styled secondary consorts: the Joogiya clan, one son, Abai;

sentences.zh: *鈕祜祿氏，子二，湯古代、塔拜；

translations.literal: *the Niohuru clan, two sons Tanggo and Tabai;
translations.idiomatic: The Niohuru clan, two sons, Tanggo and Tabai;

sentences.zh: *嘉穆瑚覺羅氏，子二，巴布泰、巴布海，女三，下嫁布占泰、達啟、蘇納；

translations.literal: *the Giamuhu Gioro clan, two sons Babutai and Babuhai, three daughters who married downward to Bushan, Daqi, and Suna;
translations.idiomatic: The Giamuhu Gioro clan, two sons, Babutai and Babuhai, and three daughters who married Bushan, Daqi, and Suna;

sentences.zh: *西林覺羅氏，子一，賴慕布；

translations.literal: *the Silin Gioro clan, one son Laimubu;
translations.idiomatic: The Silin Gioro clan, one son, Laimubu;

sentences.zh: *伊爾根覺羅氏，女一，下嫁鄂托伊。

translations.literal: *the Yirgen Gioro clan, one daughter who married downward to Etooi.
translations.idiomatic: The Yirgen Gioro clan, one daughter who married Etooi.

sentences.zh: 太宗孝端文皇后，博爾濟吉特氏，科爾沁貝勒莽古思女。

translations.literal: Empress Xiaoduan the Literary of Taizong, of the Borjigit clan, was the daughter of Manggas, beile of Khorchin.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's Empress Xiaoduan the Literary, of the Borjigit clan, was the daughter of Manggas, beile of Khorchin.

sentences.zh: 歲甲寅四月，來歸，太祖命太宗親迎，至輝發扈爾奇山城，大宴成禮。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the year jiayin she came in marriage; Taizu ordered Taizong to welcome her in person, and at Hu'erqi Mountain City in Huifa a great feast completed the rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the jiayin year she arrived as bride; Taizu ordered Taizong to meet her in person, and at Hu'erqi Mountain City in Huifa a great feast completed the wedding.

sentences.zh: 天聰間，后母科爾沁大妃屢來朝，上迎勞，錫賚有加禮，

translations.literal: During the Tiancong reign the empress's mother, the Khorchin grand consort, repeatedly came to court; the sovereign welcomed and comforted her and bestowed gifts with added ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiancong reign the empress's mother, the Khorchin grand consort, came to court repeatedly; the emperor welcomed her with honors and lavished gifts upon her.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，上建尊號，后亦正位中宮。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde, when the sovereign established his honorific title, the empress also took her proper place in the central palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongde, when he assumed his reign title, the empress also took her rightful place as mistress of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 二年，大妃復來朝，上迎宴。

translations.literal: In the second year the grand consort came to court again; the sovereign welcomed her with a feast.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the grand consort came to court again, and the emperor received her with a feast.

sentences.zh: 越二日，大妃設宴，上率後及貴妃、莊妃幸其行幄。

translations.literal: Two days later the grand consort gave a feast; the sovereign led the empress, the imperial consort, and Consort Zhuang to visit her traveling tent.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later the grand consort gave a feast, and the emperor led the empress, the imperial consort, and Consort Zhuang to her traveling tent.

sentences.zh: 尋命追封後父莽古思和碩福親王，立碑於墓，封大妃為和碩福妃，使大學士范文程等冊封。

translations.literal: Soon he ordered the empress's father Manggas to be posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of the Commandery of the First Rank of Fu, with a stele erected at his tomb; the grand consort was enfeoffed as Princess of the Commandery of the First Rank of Fu, and Grand Secretary Fan Wencheng and others were sent to invest her by patent.
translations.idiomatic: He soon ordered the empress's father Manggas posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of the Commandery of the First Rank of Fu, with a stele set up at his tomb; the grand consort was made Princess of the Commandery of the First Rank of Fu, and Grand Secretary Fan Wencheng and others were dispatched to invest her.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，尊為皇太后。

translations.literal: When Shizu ascended the throne, she was honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu came to the throne, she was honored as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 順治六年四月乙巳，崩，年五十一。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Shunzhi, on yisi in the fourth month she died, aged fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Shunzhi, on yisi in the fourth month she died, aged fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 七年，上諡。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the sovereign conferred a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the emperor conferred her posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 雍正、乾隆累加諡，曰孝端正敬仁懿哲順慈僖莊敏輔天協聖文皇后。

translations.literal: Under Yongzheng and Qianlong additional honorifics were repeatedly added, so that she was called Empress Xiaoduan Zhengjing Renyi Zhezhe Shun Ci Xi Zhuangmin Futian Xiesheng Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzheng and Qianlong added further honorifics until she was styled Empress Xiaoduan Zhengjing Renyi Zhezhe Shun Ci Xi Zhuangmin Futian Xiesheng Wen.

sentences.zh: 女三，下嫁額哲、奇塔特、巴雅思祜朗。

translations.literal: Daughters, three, who married downward to Eje, Qitata, and Bayasihulang.
translations.idiomatic: She had three daughters, who married Eje, Qitata, and Bayasihulang.

sentences.zh: 孝莊文皇后，博爾濟吉特氏，科爾沁貝勒寨桑女，孝端皇后侄也。

translations.literal: Empress Xiaozhuang the Literary, of the Borjigit clan, was the daughter of Zaisang, beile of Khorchin, and a niece of Empress Xiaoduan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaozhuang the Literary, of the Borjigit clan, was the daughter of Zaisang, beile of Khorchin, and a niece of Empress Xiaoduan.

sentences.zh: 二月，來歸，

translations.literal: In the second month she came in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month she arrived as bride.

sentences.zh: 封永福宮莊妃。

translations.literal: She was enfeoffed as Consort Zhuang of the Yongfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: She was made Consort Zhuang of the Yongfu Palace.

sentences.zh: 三年正月甲午，世祖生。

translations.literal: On jiawu in the first month of the third year Shizu was born.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu in the first month of the third year Shizu was born.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，尊為皇太后，

translations.literal: When Shizu ascended the throne, she was honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu came to the throne, she was honored as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 順治十一年，贈太后父寨桑和碩忠親王，母賢妃。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Shunzhi, the empress dowager's father Zaisang was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of the First Rank of Zhong, and her mother as Worthy Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Shunzhi, her father Zaisang was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of the First Rank of Zhong, and her mother as Worthy Consort.

sentences.zh: 十三年二月，太后萬壽，上制詩三十首以獻。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirteenth year, on the empress dowager's birthday, the sovereign composed thirty poems and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the thirteenth year, for the empress dowager's birthday, the emperor composed thirty poems and presented them to her.

sentences.zh: 上承太后訓，撰內則衍義，並為序以進。

translations.literal: Following the empress dowager's instruction, the sovereign compiled the Extended Meaning of the Inner Rules and wrote a preface to present it.
translations.idiomatic: At her instruction he compiled the Extended Meaning of the Inner Rules and wrote a preface presenting it to her.

sentences.zh: 聖祖即位，尊為太皇太后。

translations.literal: When Shengzu ascended the throne, she was honored as grand empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Shengzu came to the throne, she was honored as grand empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 國初故事，后妃，王、貝勒福晉，貝子、公夫人，皆令命婦更番入侍，至太后始命罷之。

translations.literal: By the custom of the founding of the state, empresses and consorts, the fujin of princes and beiles, and the ladies of beizi and dukes were all ordered to take turns in attendance as titled ladies; only with the empress dowager was the practice abolished.
translations.idiomatic: By an early custom of the dynasty, empresses and consorts, the fujin of princes and beiles, and the wives of beizi and dukes had all been required to take turns in attendance; it was the empress dowager who ordered the practice abolished.

sentences.zh: 宮中守祖宗制，不蓄漢女。

translations.literal: Within the palace the ancestral regulation was kept and Han women were not kept.
translations.idiomatic: The palace kept the ancestral rule and did not keep Han women.

sentences.zh: 上命儒臣譯《大學衍義》進太后，太后稱善，賜賚有加。

translations.literal: The sovereign ordered Confucian officials to translate the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning and present it to the empress dowager; the empress dowager praised it and bestowed rewards with added generosity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Confucian scholars translate the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning and present it to her; she praised it and rewarded them generously.

sentences.zh: 太后不預政，朝廷有黜陟，上多告而後行。

translations.literal: The empress dowager did not participate in government; when the court had dismissals and appointments, the sovereign mostly informed her before acting.
translations.idiomatic: She did not take part in government, but when the court made appointments and dismissals the emperor usually informed her before acting.

sentences.zh: 嘗勉上曰：「祖宗騎射開基，武備不可弛。

translations.literal: She once exhorted the sovereign, saying, "Our ancestors founded the state through mounted archery; military readiness must not be relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: She once urged him, "Our ancestors founded the state through mounted archery; military readiness must never be neglected.

sentences.zh: 用人行政，務敬以承天，虛公裁決。」

translations.literal: In employing men and administering affairs, strive to be reverent in receiving Heaven's mandate and to decide with impartial openness."
translations.idiomatic: In appointing men and governing affairs, be reverent before Heaven and decide with impartial fairness."

sentences.zh: 又作書以誡曰：「古稱為君難。

translations.literal: She also wrote a letter of admonition, saying, "The ancients said that being a ruler is hard.
translations.idiomatic: She also wrote a letter of admonition: "The ancients said that to be a ruler is hard.

sentences.zh: 蒼生至衆，天子以一身臨其上，生養撫育，莫不引領，必深思得衆得國之道，使四海咸登康阜，綿歷數於無疆，惟休。

translations.literal: The common people are exceedingly numerous; the Son of Heaven stands alone above them, nourishing and cherishing them, and all stretch their necks in expectation. You must deeply ponder the way to win the people and win the state, so that within the four seas all may reach prosperity, and the dynastic fortune may extend without limit—this alone is blessed.
translations.idiomatic: The people are countless; the Son of Heaven stands alone over them, nourishing and cherishing them, and all look to him in hope. You must deeply consider how to win the people and secure the state, so that all within the four seas may prosper and the dynastic fortune endure without end—this alone is blessedness.

sentences.zh: 汝尚寬裕慈仁，溫良恭敬，慎乃威儀，謹爾出話，夙夜恪勤，以祗承祖考遺緒，俾予亦無疚於厥心。」

translations.literal: You should still be generous and benevolent, gentle and respectful, careful in your bearing, cautious in your speech, diligent day and night, reverently to inherit the legacy of the ancestors, so that I too may have no regret in my heart."
translations.idiomatic: Be generous and benevolent, gentle and respectful; guard your bearing, weigh your words, and labor diligently day and night to inherit the legacy of your forebears, so that I too may have no regret in my heart."

sentences.zh: 十九年四月，上撰大德景福頌進太后。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the nineteenth year the sovereign composed the Ode to Great Virtue and Auspicious Blessing and presented it to the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the nineteenth year the emperor composed the Ode to Great Virtue and Auspicious Blessing and presented it to her.

sentences.zh: 二十年，上復奉太后幸湯泉。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year the sovereign again escorted the empress dowager to the hot springs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he again escorted her to the hot springs.

sentences.zh: 雲南平，上詣太后宮奏捷。

translations.literal: When Yunnan was pacified, the sovereign went to the empress dowager's palace to report victory.
translations.idiomatic: When Yunnan was pacified, he went to her palace to report the victory.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，上詣奉天謁陵，途次屢奏書問安，使獻方物，奏曰：「臣到盛京，親網得鰱、𩺀，浸以羊脂，山中野燒，自落榛實及山核桃，朝鮮所進柿餅、松、栗、銀杏，附使進上，伏乞俯賜一笑，不勝欣幸。」

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year the sovereign went to Fengtian to visit the tombs; on the way he repeatedly submitted memorial letters asking after her health and sent tribute goods, memorializing: "Your servant reached Shengjing and with his own net caught silver carp and whitefish, soaked them in mutton fat, gathered in the mountain wilds what fell from the hazel and mountain walnut trees, and also the persimmon cakes, pine nuts, chestnuts, and ginkgo sent from Korea—all sent by messenger for presentation; I humbly beg you to deign a smile; I am beyond measure delighted."
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he went to Fengtian to visit the tombs; along the way he repeatedly sent letters asking after her health and dispatched tribute, writing: "I have reached Shengjing and with my own net caught silver carp and whitefish, soaked them in mutton fat, gathered fallen hazelnuts and mountain walnuts from the hills, and also the persimmon cakes, pine nuts, chestnuts, and ginkgo sent from Korea—all sent by messenger for your enjoyment; I humbly beg you to accept them with a smile; nothing could delight me more."

sentences.zh: 二十二年夏，奉太后出古北口避暑。

translations.literal: In the summer of the twenty-second year he escorted the empress dowager out through Gubeikou to escape the heat.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the twenty-second year he escorted her out through Gubeikou to escape the heat.

sentences.zh: 秋，幸五台山，至龍泉關。

translations.literal: In autumn he visited Mount Wutai and reached Longquan Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn he visited Mount Wutai and reached Longquan Pass.

sentences.zh: 上以長城嶺峻絕，試輦不能陟，奏太后。

translations.literal: Because the Great Wall Ridge was steep and precipitous, a trial of the palanquin showed it could not be ascended; he reported this to the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Great Wall Ridge was steep and sheer, a trial showed the palanquin could not be taken up it, and he reported this to her.

sentences.zh: 次日，太后輦登嶺，路數折不可上，太后乃還龍泉關，命上代禮諸寺。

translations.literal: The next day the empress dowager's palanquin ascended the ridge, but the road turned again and again and could not be climbed; the empress dowager then returned to Longquan Pass and ordered the sovereign to perform rites at the temples in her stead.
translations.idiomatic: The next day her palanquin set out up the ridge, but the road twisted too steeply to be climbed; she turned back to Longquan Pass and ordered him to perform rites at the temples on her behalf.

sentences.zh: 二十四年夏，上出塞避暑，次博洛和屯，聞太后不豫，即馳還京師，太后疾良已。

translations.literal: In the summer of the twenty-fourth year the sovereign went beyond the frontier to escape the heat and halted at Boluohetun; hearing that the empress dowager was unwell, he immediately galloped back to the capital, and the empress dowager's illness had already greatly improved.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the twenty-fourth year he went beyond the frontier to escape the heat and halted at Boluohetun; when he heard she was unwell he raced back to the capital, and by then she was already much recovered.

sentences.zh: 二十六年九月，太后疾復作，上晝夜在視。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the twenty-sixth year the empress dowager's illness recurred; the sovereign attended her day and night.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the twenty-sixth year her illness returned, and he attended her day and night.

sentences.zh: 十二月，步禱天壇，請減算以益太后。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he walked in prayer at the Temple of Heaven, asking to reduce his own allotted years to extend the empress dowager's life.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he walked in prayer at the Temple of Heaven, asking to shorten his own allotted years to lengthen hers.

sentences.zh: 讀祝，上泣，陪祀諸王大臣皆泣。

translations.literal: When the prayer text was read, the sovereign wept, and the princes and ministers attending the sacrifice all wept.
translations.idiomatic: When the prayer was read, he wept, and the princes and ministers attending the rite wept with him.

sentences.zh: 太后疾大漸，命上曰：「太宗奉安久，不可為我輕動。

translations.literal: As the empress dowager's illness grew grave, she commanded the sovereign, saying, "Taizong has long rested in his tomb; you must not lightly move him on my account.
translations.idiomatic: As her illness grew grave, she told him, "Taizong has long rested in his tomb; you must not disturb him on my account.

sentences.zh: 況我心戀汝父子，當於孝陵近地安厝，我心始無憾。」

translations.literal: Moreover my heart is bound to you, father and son; I should be laid to rest near the Xiaoling mausoleum, and only then will my heart be without regret."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover my heart is bound to you and your father; lay me to rest near the Xiaoling mausoleum, and only then will I be at peace."

sentences.zh: 己巳，崩，年七十五。

translations.literal: On jisi she died, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi she died, aged seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 上哀慟，欲於宮中持服二十七月，王大臣屢疏請遵遺誥，以日易月，始從之。

translations.literal: The sovereign grieved deeply and wished to wear mourning in the palace for twenty-seven months; the princes and ministers repeatedly memorialized asking that the testamentary command be followed and mourning be reckoned by days in place of months, and only then did he consent.
translations.idiomatic: He grieved deeply and wished to mourn in the palace for twenty-seven months; the princes and ministers repeatedly memorialized that he follow her testament and observe mourning by days in place of months, and at last he consented.

sentences.zh: 命撤太后所居宮移建昌瑞山孝陵近地，號「暫安奉殿」。

translations.literal: He ordered the palace where the empress dowager had lived to be dismantled and rebuilt near the Xiaoling mausoleum on Changrui Mountain, called the "Temporary Hall of Repose and Offering."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered her residence dismantled and rebuilt near the Xiaoling mausoleum on Changrui Mountain, naming it the Temporary Hall of Repose and Offering.

sentences.zh: 二十七年四月，奉太后梓宮詣昌瑞山。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twenty-seventh year he escorted the empress dowager's coffin to Changrui Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the twenty-seventh year he escorted her coffin to Changrui Mountain.

sentences.zh: 自是，歲必詣謁。

translations.literal: From then on, every year he went to pay his respects.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he visited every year to pay his respects.

sentences.zh: 雍正三年十二月，世宗即其地起陵，曰昭西陵。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongzheng, in the twelfth month Shizong raised a mausoleum on that site, called the Zhaoxi Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongzheng, in the twelfth month Shizong built a mausoleum on that site, naming it the Zhaoxi Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 聖祖親政，上太后徽號，國有慶，必加上。

translations.literal: When Shengzu personally took government, he conferred honorific titles on the empress dowager, and whenever the state had a celebration he always added to them.
translations.idiomatic: When Shengzu took personal rule, he conferred honorific titles on her, and whenever the state celebrated a great event he added to them.

sentences.zh: 至聖祖以雲南平，奏捷，定徽號曰昭聖慈壽恭簡安懿章慶敦惠溫莊康和仁宣弘靖太皇太后，初奉安上諡。

translations.literal: When Shengzu reported victory upon the pacification of Yunnan, the honorific title was fixed as Grand Empress Dowager Zhaosheng Cishou Gongjian Anyi Zhangqing Dunhui Wenzhuang Kanghe Renxuan Hongjing, and at the initial enshrinement the sovereign conferred a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: When Shengzu reported victory after the pacification of Yunnan, her honorific title was fixed as Grand Empress Dowager Zhaosheng Cishou Gongjian Anyi Zhangqing Dunhui Wenzhuang Kanghe Renxuan Hongjing, and at her initial enshrinement he conferred her posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 雍正、乾隆累加諡，曰孝莊仁宣誠憲恭懿至德純徽翊天啟聖文皇后。

translations.literal: Under Yongzheng and Qianlong additional honorifics were repeatedly added, so that she was called Empress Xiaozhuang Renxuan Chengxian Gongyi Zhide Chunhui Yitian Qisheng Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzheng and Qianlong added further honorifics until she was styled Empress Xiaozhuang Renxuan Chengxian Gongyi Zhide Chunhui Yitian Qisheng Wen.

sentences.zh: 子一，世祖。

translations.literal: Sons, one: Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: She bore one son, Shizu.

sentences.zh: 女三，下嫁弼爾塔哈爾、色布騰、鏗吉爾格。

translations.literal: Daughters, three, who married downward to Birtakhar, Sebuteng, and Kengjierge.
translations.idiomatic: She had three daughters, who married Birtakhar, Sebuteng, and Kengjierge.

sentences.zh: 敏惠恭和元妃，博爾濟吉特氏，孝莊皇后姊也，

translations.literal: Primary Consort Minhui Gonghe, of the Borjigit clan, was the elder sister of Empress Xiaozhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Primary Consort Minhui Gonghe, of the Borjigit clan, was Empress Xiaozhuang's elder sister.

sentences.zh: 來歸，

translations.literal: She came in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: She arrived as bride.

sentences.zh: 封關睢宮宸妃。

translations.literal: She was enfeoffed as Imperial Consort Chen of the Guansui Palace.
translations.idiomatic: She was made Imperial Consort Chen of the Guansui Palace.

sentences.zh: 妃有寵於太宗，生子，為大赦，子二歲而殤，未命名。

translations.literal: The consort enjoyed Taizong's favor; when she bore a son a general amnesty was declared, but the child died at two years without being given a name.
translations.idiomatic: She enjoyed Taizong's favor; when she bore a son he declared a general amnesty, but the child died at two without ever being named.

sentences.zh: 六年九月，太宗方伐明，聞妃病而還，未至，妃已薨。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the sixth year Taizong was campaigning against the Ming when he heard the consort was ill and returned; before he arrived, the consort had already died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the sixth year Taizong was campaigning against the Ming when he heard she was ill and turned back; before he arrived, she had already died.

sentences.zh: 上慟甚，一日忽迷惘，自午至酉始瘥，乃悔曰：「天生朕為撫世安民，豈為一婦人哉？

translations.literal: The sovereign grieved deeply; one day he suddenly fell into confusion and only recovered from noon until you; then he regretted and said, "Heaven bore me to comfort the age and settle the people—was it for one woman?
translations.idiomatic: He grieved deeply; one day he suddenly fell into a daze and did not recover until evening; then he reproached himself, "Heaven made me to comfort the age and settle the people—was it for the sake of one woman?

sentences.zh: 朕不能自持，天地祖宗特示譴也。」

translations.literal: That I could not restrain myself—Heaven, Earth, and the ancestors specially showed their reproof."
translations.idiomatic: That I could not restrain myself—Heaven, Earth, and the ancestors were reproving me."

sentences.zh: 上仍悲悼不已。

translations.literal: The sovereign still mourned without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he still mourned without end.

sentences.zh: 諸王大臣請出獵，遂獵蒲河。

translations.literal: The princes and ministers asked that he go out hunting, and he hunted on the Pu River.
translations.idiomatic: The princes and ministers urged him to go hunting, and he hunted on the Pu River.

sentences.zh: 還過妃墓，復大慟。

translations.literal: On the return he passed the consort's tomb and again grieved deeply.
translations.idiomatic: On the way back he passed her tomb and grieved afresh.

sentences.zh: 妃母和碩賢妃來吊，上命內大臣掖輿臨妃墓。

translations.literal: The consort's mother, Princess of the Commandery of the First Rank of Xian, came to offer condolences; the sovereign ordered inner ministers to support her palanquin to the consort's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother, Princess of the Commandery of the First Rank of Xian, came to mourn; the emperor ordered inner ministers to support her palanquin to the consort's tomb.

sentences.zh: 郡王阿達禮、輔國公扎哈納當妃喪作樂，皆坐奪爵。

translations.literal: Prince of the Commandery Adali and Assistant State Defender Zahana made music during the consort's mourning; both were punished by deprivation of rank.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of the Commandery Adali and Assistant State Defender Zahana made music during her mourning; both were stripped of their titles.

sentences.zh: 懿靖大貴妃，博爾濟吉特氏，阿霸垓郡王額齊格諾顏女，

translations.literal: Grand Imperial Noble Consort Yijing, of the Borjigit clan, was the daughter of Eqiger Noyan, prince of the commandery of Abagai.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Imperial Noble Consort Yijing, of the Borjigit clan, was the daughter of Eqiger Noyan, prince of the commandery of Abagai.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，封麟趾宮貴妃。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde, she was enfeoffed as Imperial Consort of the Linzhi Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongde, she was made Imperial Consort of the Linzhi Palace.

sentences.zh: 四年，額齊格諾顏及其妻福晉來朝，妃率諸王、貝勒迎宴。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Eqiger Noyan and his wife the fujin came to court; the consort led the princes and beiles to welcome and feast them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Eqiger Noyan and his wife came to court; the consort led the princes and beiles to welcome and feast them.

sentences.zh: 次日，上賜宴清寧宮，福晉入見，稱上外姑，

translations.literal: The next day the sovereign gave a banquet at Qingning Palace; the fujin entered for audience and addressed the sovereign as waigu.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor gave a banquet at Qingning Palace; the fujin entered for audience and addressed him with the honored title of a maternal in-law.

sentences.zh: 世祖加尊封，

translations.literal: Shizu added further honored enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu added further honors.

sentences.zh: 薨，聖祖侍太后臨奠。

translations.literal: She died; Shengzu attended the empress dowager in going to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: She died; Shengzu accompanied the empress dowager to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 子一，博穆博果爾。

translations.literal: Sons, one: Bumbutai.
translations.idiomatic: She bore one son, Bumbutai.

sentences.zh: 女一，下嫁噶爾瑪索諾木。

translations.literal: Daughters, one, who married downward to Gaermasuonuomu.
translations.idiomatic: She had one daughter, who married Gaermasuonuomu.

sentences.zh: 又撫蒙古女，嫁噶爾瑪德參，濟旺子也。

translations.literal: She also raised a Mongol girl, who married Gaermadecan, son of Jiwang.
translations.idiomatic: She also raised a Mongol girl who married Gaermadecan, son of Jiwang.

sentences.zh: 康惠淑妃，博爾濟吉特氏，阿霸垓塔布囊博第塞楚祜爾女，

translations.literal: Imperial Consort Kanghui Shufei, of the Borjigit clan, was the daughter of Tabunang Bodisechuhu'er of Abagai.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Consort Kanghui Shufei, of the Borjigit clan, was the daughter of Tabunang Bodisechuhu'er of Abagai.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，封衍慶宮淑妃。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde, she was enfeoffed as Imperial Consort Shufei of the Yansing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongde, she was made Imperial Consort Shufei of the Yansing Palace.

sentences.zh: 撫蒙古女，上命睿親王多爾袞娶焉，

translations.literal: She raised a Mongol girl; the sovereign ordered Prince Regent Dorgon to marry her.
translations.idiomatic: She raised a Mongol girl, and the emperor ordered Prince Regent Dorgon to marry her.

sentences.zh: 順治九年，加尊封，前懿靖大貴妃薨。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Shunzhi, Further honored enfeoffment was added; previously Grand Imperial Noble Consort Yijing had died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Shunzhi, Further honors were added; by then Grand Imperial Noble Consort Yijing had already died.

sentences.zh: 太宗諸妃：*元妃，鈕祜祿氏，弘毅公額亦都女，子一，洛博會；

translations.literal: Taizong's consorts: *Primary Consort, of the Niohuru clan, daughter of Hongyi Duke Eyidu, one son: Luobohui;
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's consorts: Primary Consort, of the Niohuru clan, daughter of Hongyi Duke Eyidu, one son, Luobohui;

sentences.zh: *繼妃，烏拉納喇氏，子二，豪格、洛格，女一，下嫁旺第。

translations.literal: *Succession Consort, of the Ula Nara clan, two sons: Hooge and Luo'ge, one daughter who married downward to Wangdi.
translations.idiomatic: Succession Consort, of the Ula Nara clan, two sons, Hooge and Luo'ge, and one daughter who married Wangdi.

sentences.zh: 稱側妃者二：*葉赫納喇氏，子一，碩塞；

translations.literal: Two called side consorts: *Yehe Nara clan, one son: Shuose;
translations.idiomatic: Two were called side consorts: Yehe Nara clan, one son, Shuose;

sentences.zh: *扎魯特博爾濟吉特氏，女二，下嫁誇扎、哈尚。

translations.literal: *Jarud Borjigit clan, two daughters who married downward to Kuazha and Hashang.
translations.idiomatic: Jarud Borjigit clan, two daughters who married Kuazha and Hashang.

sentences.zh: 稱庶妃者六：*納喇氏，子一，高塞，女二，下嫁輝塞、拉哈；

translations.literal: Six called lesser consorts: *Nara clan, one son: Gaose, two daughters who married downward to Huise and Laha;
translations.idiomatic: Six were called lesser consorts: Nara clan, one son, Gaose, and two daughters who married Huise and Laha;

sentences.zh: *奇壘氏，察哈爾部人，女一，下嫁吳應熊；

translations.literal: *Qilei clan, a woman of the Chahar tribe, one daughter who married downward to Wu Yingxiong;
translations.idiomatic: Qilei clan, of the Chahar tribe, one daughter who married Wu Yingxiong;

sentences.zh: *顏札氏，子一，葉布舒；

translations.literal: *Yanzha clan, one son: Yeibushu;
translations.idiomatic: Yanzha clan, one son, Yeibushu;

sentences.zh: *伊爾根覺羅氏，子一，常舒；

translations.literal: *Irgen Gioro clan, one son: Changshu;
translations.idiomatic: Irgen Gioro clan, one son, Changshu;

sentences.zh: *其二不知氏族，一生子，韜塞；

translations.literal: *Of the remaining two their clans are unknown; one bore a son: Taose;
translations.idiomatic: Of the other two the clans are unknown; one bore a son, Taose;

sentences.zh: 一生女，下嫁班第。

translations.literal: One bore a daughter who married downward to Bandi.
translations.idiomatic: The other bore a daughter who married Bandi.

sentences.zh: 世祖廢后，博爾濟吉特氏，科爾沁卓禮克圖親王吳克善女，孝莊文皇后姪也。

translations.literal: The deposed empress of Shizu, of the Borjigit clan, was the daughter of Wu Keqan, Prince of the Commandery of the First Rank of Zhuoliketu of Horqin, and was a niece of Empress Xiaozhuang Wen.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed empress of Shizu, of the Borjigit clan, was the daughter of Wu Keqan, Prince of the Commandery of the First Rank of Zhuoliketu of Horqin, and a niece of Empress Xiaozhuang Wen.

sentences.zh: 后麗而慧，睿親王多爾袞攝政，為世祖聘焉。

translations.literal: The empress was beautiful and clever; Prince Regent Dorgon held the regency and arranged her betrothal for Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was beautiful and clever; while Prince Regent Dorgon held the regency, he arranged her betrothal to Shizu.

sentences.zh: 順治八年八月，冊為皇后。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Shunzhi, in the eighth month she was invested as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Shunzhi, in the eighth month she was invested as empress.

sentences.zh: 上好簡樸，后則嗜奢侈，又妒，積與上忤。

translations.literal: The sovereign favored simplicity; the empress, however, loved luxury and was jealous, and over time she repeatedly clashed with him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor favored simplicity, but the empress loved luxury and was jealous; over time the two grew steadily at odds.

sentences.zh: 十年八月，上命大學士馮銓等上前代廢后故事，銓等疏諫，上嚴拒，諭以「無能，故當廢」，責諸臣沽名。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the tenth year the sovereign ordered Grand Secretaries Feng Quan and others to bring forward precedents from earlier ages for deposing an empress; Quan and the others memorialized in remonstrance, but the sovereign sternly refused, instructing that "she is incompetent and therefore should be deposed," and rebuked the ministers for seeking a reputation.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the tenth year the emperor ordered Grand Secretaries Feng Quan and others to bring forward precedents for deposing an empress; Quan and the others memorialized in protest, but the emperor sternly refused, declaring that "she is incompetent and must be deposed," and rebuked the ministers for courting a reputation.

sentences.zh: 即日奏皇太后，降后為靜妃，改居側宮，下禮部，禮部尚書胡世安、侍郎呂崇烈、高珩疏請慎重詳審，禮部員外郎孔允樾及御史宗敦一、潘朝選、陳棐、張璟、杜果、聶玠、張嘉、李敬、劉秉政、陳自德、祖永傑、高爾位、白尚登、祖建明各具疏力爭。

translations.literal: That same day he reported to the empress dowager, demoted the empress to Consort Jing, and moved her to a side palace; he sent the matter to the Ministry of Rites. Minister of Rites Hu Shi'an and Vice Ministers Lu Chonglie and Gao Heng memorialized asking for careful and thorough review; Section Director Kong Yunyu of the Ministry of Rites and Censors Zong Dunyi, Pan Chaoxuan, Chen Fei, Zhang Jing, Du Guo, Nie Jie, Zhang Jia, Li Jing, Liu Bingzheng, Chen Zide, Zu Yongjie, Gao Erwei, Bai Shangdeng, and Zu Jianming each submitted separate memorials arguing forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he reported to the empress dowager, demoted the empress to Consort Jing, and moved her to a side palace, then referred the matter to the Ministry of Rites. Minister Hu Shi'an and Vice Ministers Lu Chonglie and Gao Heng pleaded for careful review; Section Director Kong Yunyu and censors Zong Dunyi, Pan Chaoxuan, Chen Fei, Zhang Jing, Du Guo, Nie Jie, Zhang Jia, Li Jing, Liu Bingzheng, Chen Zide, Zu Yongjie, Gao Erwei, Bai Shangdeng, and Zu Jianming each submitted memorials arguing forcefully against the decision.

sentences.zh: 允樾言尤切，略言：「皇后正位三年，未聞失德，特以『無能』二字定廢嫡之案，何以服皇后之心？

translations.literal: Yunyu's words were especially forceful; in summary he said, "The empress has held the primary position for three years, and no loss of virtue has been heard; to settle a case of deposing the primary consort on the two words 'incompetent' alone—how can this satisfy the empress's heart?
translations.idiomatic: Yunyu spoke most forcefully, arguing in essence: "The empress has held her place for three years without any reported lapse in virtue; to settle a case of deposing the primary consort on the single charge of 'incompetence'—how can that satisfy the empress?

sentences.zh: 何以服天下後世之心？

translations.literal: How can it satisfy the hearts of all under Heaven and of later ages?
translations.idiomatic: How can it satisfy the court, the realm, and posterity?

sentences.zh: 君后猶父母，父欲出母，即心知母過，猶涕泣以諫；

translations.literal: Sovereign and empress are like father and mother; if a father wishes to cast out the mother, even knowing the mother's fault he still weeps and remonstrates;
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign and empress are like father and mother; if a father wishes to cast out the mother, even knowing she is at fault he still weeps and remonstrates;

sentences.zh: 況不知母過何事，安忍緘口而不為母請命？」

translations.literal: How much more when one does not know what fault the mother has committed—how can one bear to keep silent and not plead for the mother's life?"
translations.idiomatic: How much more when one does not even know what fault she has committed—how can one bear to keep silent and not plead for her?"

sentences.zh: 上命諸王、貝勒、大臣集議，議仍以皇后位中宮，而別立東西兩宮。

translations.literal: The sovereign ordered the princes, beiles, and ministers to assemble for deliberation; they deliberated that the empress should still occupy the central palace, while separate eastern and western palaces should be established.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the princes, beiles, and ministers to confer; they proposed that the empress remain in the central palace while separate eastern and western palaces be established.

sentences.zh: 上不許，令再議，並責允樾覆奏，允樾疏引罪，諸王大臣再議，請從上指，於是后竟廢。

translations.literal: The sovereign did not consent and ordered further deliberation; he also ordered Yunyu to reply in a memorial, and Yunyu submitted a memorial accepting blame; the princes and ministers deliberated again and asked to follow the sovereign's intent, and so the empress was finally deposed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused and ordered them to deliberate again; he also required Yunyu to reply in a memorial, and Yunyu submitted one accepting blame. When the princes and ministers met again they asked to follow the emperor's will, and the empress was at last deposed.

sentences.zh: 孝惠章皇后，博爾濟吉特氏，科爾沁貝勒綽爾濟女。

translations.literal: Empress Xiaohui Zhang, of the Borjigit clan, was the daughter of Beile Chuo'erji of Horqin.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaohui Zhang, of the Borjigit clan, was the daughter of Beile Chuo'erji of Horqin.

sentences.zh: 順治十一年五月，聘為妃，六月，冊為后。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Shunzhi, in the fifth month she was betrothed as consort; in the sixth month she was invested as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Shunzhi, in the fifth month she was betrothed as consort; in the sixth month she was invested as empress.

sentences.zh: 貴妃董鄂氏方幸，后又不當上恉。

translations.literal: Imperial Noble Consort Donggo was then in favor, and the empress again did not accord with the sovereign's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Noble Consort Donggo was then in favor, and the empress again failed to please the emperor.

sentences.zh: 十五年正月，皇太后不豫，上責后禮節疏闕，命停應進中宮箋表，下諸王、貝勒、大臣議行。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year the empress dowager fell ill; the sovereign blamed the empress for lapses in ritual propriety, ordered a halt to the memorials and reports due from the central palace, and sent the matter down to the princes, beiles, and ministers for deliberation on how to proceed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifteenth year the empress dowager fell ill; the emperor blamed the empress for lapses in ritual propriety, halted the memorials due from the central palace, and referred the matter to the princes, beiles, and ministers for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 三月，以皇太后旨，如舊制封進。

translations.literal: In the third month, by the empress dowager's order, honors were submitted according to the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, at the empress dowager's order, the honors were submitted again according to the old regulations.

sentences.zh: 聖祖即位，尊為皇太后，居慈仁宮。

translations.literal: When Shengzu acceded to the throne, she was honored as empress dowager and resided in the Ciren Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Shengzu acceded to the throne, she was honored as empress dowager and took up residence in the Ciren Palace.

sentences.zh: 上奉太皇太后謁孝陵，幸盛京，謁福陵、昭陵，出古北口避暑，幸五臺山，皆奉太后侍行，

translations.literal: The sovereign attended the grand empress dowager in paying respects at the Xiaoling Mausoleum, visited Shengjing, paid respects at the Fuling and Zhaoling mausoleums, went out through Gubeikou to escape the summer heat, and visited Wutai Mountain—all times attending the empress dowager in accompanying the journey.
translations.idiomatic: Whether visiting the Xiaoling Mausoleum with the grand empress dowager, traveling to Shengjing, paying respects at the Fuling and Zhaoling mausoleums, leaving through Gubeikou to escape the summer heat, or visiting Wutai Mountain, the emperor always had the empress dowager accompany him.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十二年，上奉太皇太后出塞，太后未侍行，中途射得鹿，斷尾漬以鹽，並親選榛實，進太后。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Kangxi, when the sovereign attended the grand empress dowager beyond the frontier, the empress dowager did not accompany the journey; midway he shot a deer, cut off its tail and cured it with salt, and personally selected hazelnuts, presenting them to the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Kangxi, on one journey beyond the frontier with the grand empress dowager, the empress dowager did not go along; midway the emperor shot a deer, cut off its tail and cured it with salt, personally selected hazelnuts, and sent them to the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，太皇太后不豫，太后朝夕奉侍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the grand empress dowager fell ill; the empress dowager attended her morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year the grand empress dowager fell ill, and the empress dowager attended her morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 及太皇太后崩，太后悲痛。

translations.literal: When the grand empress dowager died, the empress dowager was stricken with grief.
translations.idiomatic: When the grand empress dowager died, the empress dowager was overcome with grief.

sentences.zh: 諸妃主入臨，太后慟甚，幾仆地。

translations.literal: When the consorts and ladies came to mourn, the empress dowager grieved so deeply she nearly fell to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: When the consorts and ladies came to mourn, the empress dowager grieved so deeply she nearly collapsed.

sentences.zh: 上命諸王大臣奏請太后節哀回宮，再請乃允。

translations.literal: The sovereign ordered the princes and ministers to memorialize asking the empress dowager to restrain her grief and return to the palace; only after a second request did she consent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the princes and ministers to plead with the empress dowager to restrain her grief and return to the palace; only after they asked again did she consent.

sentences.zh: 歲除，諸王大臣請太后諭上回宮，上不可。

translations.literal: At year's end the princes and ministers asked the empress dowager to instruct the sovereign to return to the palace; he would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: At year's end the princes and ministers asked the empress dowager to urge the emperor to return to the palace, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 二十七年正月，行虞祭，上命諸王大臣請太后勿往行禮，太后亦不可。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-seventh year, when the yu rites were performed, the sovereign ordered the princes and ministers to ask the empress dowager not to go to perform the rites; she too would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-seventh year, when the yu rites were performed, the emperor ordered the princes and ministers to ask the empress dowager not to attend; she too refused.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，建寧壽新宮，奉太后居焉。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year the Ningshou New Palace was built, and the empress dowager was installed to reside there.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year the Ningshou New Palace was built, and the empress dowager was installed there.

sentences.zh: 三十五年十月，上北巡，太后萬壽，上奉書稱祝。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the thirty-fifth year the sovereign toured the north; it was the empress dowager's birthday, and he sent a letter offering congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the thirty-fifth year the emperor toured the north; on the empress dowager's birthday he sent a letter of congratulation.

sentences.zh: 駐麗蘇，太后遣送衣裘，上奉書言：「時方燠，河未冰，帳房不須置火，俟嚴寒，即歡忭而服之。」

translations.literal: While encamped at Lisu, the empress dowager sent fur garments; the sovereign sent a letter saying, "The season is still warm, the rivers are not yet frozen, and the tent need not be heated; wait until the severe cold, then gladly put them on."
translations.idiomatic: While encamped at Lisu, the empress dowager sent fur garments; the emperor replied in a letter, "The season is still warm, the rivers are not yet frozen, and the tent need not be heated; wait until the bitter cold, then put them on with joy."

sentences.zh: 三十六年二月，上親征噶爾丹，駐他喇布拉克。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirty-sixth year the sovereign personally campaigned against Galdan and encamped at Talaburak.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the thirty-sixth year the emperor personally campaigned against Galdan and encamped at Talaburak.

sentences.zh: 太后以上生日，使賜金銀茶壺，上奉書拜受。

translations.literal: The empress dowager, because it was the sovereign's birthday, sent gifts of a gold and silver teapot; the sovereign sent a letter in acceptance with a bow.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's birthday the empress dowager sent a gold and silver teapot as a gift; the emperor replied with a letter of grateful acceptance.

sentences.zh: 噶爾丹既定，羣臣請上加太后徽號壽康顯寧，太后以上不受尊號，亦堅諭不受。

translations.literal: After Galdan was settled, the assembled ministers asked that the sovereign add to the empress dowager's honorific title Shoukang Xianning; the empress dowager, because the sovereign did not accept honorific titles, also firmly instructed that she would not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: After Galdan was subdued, the ministers asked that the emperor add the honorific Shoukang Xianning to the empress dowager's title; because the emperor himself refused honorific titles, she also firmly declined to accept them.

sentences.zh: 三十七年七月，奉太后幸盛京謁陵，道喀喇沁。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the thirty-seventh year he attended the empress dowager on a visit to Shengjing to pay respects at the mausoleums, passing through Kharachin.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the thirty-seventh year he accompanied the empress dowager to Shengjing to pay respects at the mausoleums, traveling by way of Kharachin.

sentences.zh: 途中以太后父母葬發庫山，距蹕路二百裡，諭內大臣索額圖擇潔地，太后遙設祭。

translations.literal: On the journey, because the empress dowager's parents were buried at Faku Mountain, two hundred li from the imperial route, he instructed Inner Minister Songgotu to select a pure site, and the empress dowager performed rites of offering from afar.
translations.idiomatic: On the journey, because the empress dowager's parents were buried at Faku Mountain, two hundred li from the imperial route, he ordered Inner Minister Songgotu to select a suitable site, and the empress dowager offered rites from afar.

sentences.zh: 十月，次奇爾賽畢喇，值太后萬壽，上詣行宮行禮，敕封太后所駐山曰壽山。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he halted at Qiersai Bila; it fell on the empress dowager's birthday, and the sovereign went to the traveling palace to perform the rites, decreeing that the mountain where the empress dowager was staying be named Shou Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he halted at Qiersai Bila on the empress dowager's birthday; the emperor went to the traveling palace to perform the rites and decreed that the mountain where she was staying be named Shou Mountain.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，上奉太后南巡。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year the sovereign attended the empress dowager on a southern tour.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year the emperor accompanied the empress dowager on a southern tour.

sentences.zh: 三十九年十月，太后六十萬壽，上製《萬壽無疆賦》，並奉佛像，珊瑚，自鳴鐘，洋鏡，東珠，珊瑚、金珀、禦風石，念珠，皮裘，羽緞，哆羅呢，沈、檀、芸、降諸香，犀玉、瑪瑙、赩、漆諸器，宋、元、明名畫，金銀、幣帛；

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the thirty-ninth year, on the empress dowager's sixtieth birthday, the sovereign composed the "Wanshou Wujiang Fu" and presented Buddha images, coral, self-ringing bells, foreign mirrors, eastern pearls, coral, golden amber, imperial wind stones, prayer beads, fur garments, feathered satin, doro ni, aloeswood, sandalwood, artemisia, and eaglewood incense, rhinoceros horn, jade, agate, cinnabar, and lacquer vessels, famous paintings of the Song, Yuan, and Ming, and gold, silver, and silks;
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the thirty-ninth year, on the empress dowager's sixtieth birthday, the emperor composed the "Wanshou Wujiang Fu" and presented Buddha images, coral, self-ringing clocks, foreign mirrors, eastern pearls, golden amber, imperial wind stones, prayer beads, fur garments, feathered satin, doro ni, aloeswood, sandalwood, artemisia, and eaglewood incense, rhinoceros horn, jade, agate, cinnabar, and lacquer vessels, famous Song, Yuan, and Ming paintings, and gold, silver, and silks;

sentences.zh: 又令膳房數米萬粒，號「萬國玉粒飯」，及餚饌、果品以獻。

translations.literal: He also ordered the imperial kitchen to count out ten thousand grains of rice, called "Wanguo Yuli Fan," along with delicacies and fruits to present.
translations.idiomatic: He also had the imperial kitchen count out ten thousand grains of rice, called "Wanguo Yuli Fan," along with delicacies and fruits as offerings.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，太后七十萬壽，亦如之。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year, on the empress dowager's seventieth birthday, it was done likewise.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year, on her seventieth birthday, he did the same.

sentences.zh: 五十六年十一月，太后不豫。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fifty-sixth year the empress dowager fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fifty-sixth year the empress dowager fell ill.

sentences.zh: 是歲，上春秋六十有四，方有疾，頭眩足腫，聞太后疾，以帕纏足，乘輭輿詣視，跪床下，捧太后手曰：「母后，臣在此！」

translations.literal: That year the sovereign was sixty-four years of age; he himself was ill, with dizziness in the head and swelling in the feet, but when he heard the empress dowager was ill he bound his feet with cloth, rode in a palanquin to visit her, knelt beside the bed, took her hand, and said, "Mother Empress, your subject is here!"
translations.idiomatic: That year the emperor was sixty-four; he himself was ill, dizzy and with swollen feet, but when he heard the empress dowager was ill he bound his feet with cloth, rode in a palanquin to see her, knelt beside the bed, took her hand, and said, "Mother Empress, I am here!"

sentences.zh: 太后張目，畏明，障以手，視上，執上手，已不能語。

translations.literal: The empress dowager opened her eyes; she feared the light and shielded it with her hand, looked at the sovereign, took his hand, but could no longer speak.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager opened her eyes; she feared the light and shielded it with her hand, looked at the emperor, took his hand, but could no longer speak.

sentences.zh: 上力疾，於蒼震門內支幄以居。

translations.literal: The sovereign, forcing himself despite illness, pitched a tent to dwell within the Cangzhen Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Despite his illness the emperor pitched a tent and stayed within the Cangzhen Gate.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，太后崩，年七十七。

translations.literal: On bingxu day the empress dowager died, aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu day the empress dowager died, aged seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 上號慟盡禮。

translations.literal: The sovereign wailed and exhausted every observance of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wailed and observed every rite of mourning.

sentences.zh: 五十七年三月，葬孝陵之東，曰孝東陵。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifty-seventh year she was buried east of the Xiaoling Mausoleum, called the Xiaodong Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifty-seventh year she was buried east of the Xiaoling Mausoleum, at what is called the Xiaodong Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 初上太后徽號，國有慶，必加上。

translations.literal: When the sovereign first granted the empress dowager an honorific title, whenever the state had a celebration additional characters were always appended.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first granted her an honorific title, additional characters were appended whenever the state celebrated a great occasion.

sentences.zh: 至雲南平定，曰仁憲恪順誠惠純淑端禧皇太后。

translations.literal: By the time Yunnan was pacified she was styled Empress Dowager Renxian Keshun Chenghui Chunshu Duanxi.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Yunnan was pacified she was styled Empress Dowager Renxian Keshun Chenghui Chunshu Duanxi.

sentences.zh: 及崩，上諡，大學士等初議誤不系世祖諡，上令至太廟、奉先殿瞻禮高皇后、文皇后神位，大學士等引罪；

translations.literal: When she died the sovereign granted a posthumous title; the grand secretaries' initial proposal wrongly failed to link it to Shizu's posthumous title, and the sovereign ordered them to go to the Imperial Ancestral Temple and the Hall for Venerating Ancestors to pay respects before the spirit tablets of Empress Gao and Empress Wen; the grand secretaries accepted blame;
translations.idiomatic: After her death the emperor granted a posthumous title; the grand secretaries' initial proposal wrongly failed to link it to Shizu's posthumous title, and the emperor ordered them to pay respects at the spirit tablets of Empress Gao and Empress Wen in the Imperial Ancestral Temple and the Hall for Venerating Ancestors; the grand secretaries accepted blame;

sentences.zh: 又以所擬諡未多留徽號字，命更議。

translations.literal: He also said the proposed posthumous title had not retained enough characters from the honorific title and ordered a new deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: He also said the proposed posthumous title retained too few characters from her honorific title and ordered them to deliberate again.

sentences.zh: 雍正、乾隆累加諡，曰孝惠仁憲端懿慈淑恭安純德順天翼聖章皇后。

translations.literal: Under Yongzheng and Qianlong additional posthumous honorifics were repeatedly added, so that she was called Empress Xiaohui Renxian Duanyi Cishu Gong'an Chunde Shuntian Yisheng Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzheng and Qianlong added further posthumous honorifics until she was styled Empress Xiaohui Renxian Duanyi Cishu Gong'an Chunde Shuntian Yisheng Zhang.

sentences.zh: 孝康章皇后，佟佳氏，少保、固山額真佟圖賴女。

translations.literal: Empress Xiaokang Zhang, of the Tunggiya clan, was the daughter of Junior Guardian and Gushan Ejen Tuwalai.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaokang Zhang, of the Tunggiya clan, was the daughter of Junior Guardian and Gushan Ejen Tuwalai.

sentences.zh: 后初入宮，為世祖妃。

translations.literal: When the empress first entered the palace she was Shizu's consort.
translations.idiomatic: When she first entered the palace she was a consort of Shizu.

sentences.zh: 春，妃詣太后宮問安，將出，衣裾有光若龍繞，太后問之，知有姙，謂近侍曰：「朕姙皇帝實有斯祥，今妃亦有是，生子必膺大福。」
