translations.literal: In spring the consort went to the empress dowager's palace to pay her respects; as she was about to leave, light like a dragon coiling appeared on the hem of her robe; the empress dowager asked about it, learned she was pregnant, and said to those near at hand, "When I was pregnant with the emperor there was truly this auspicious sign; now the consort has it too—her child will surely receive great fortune."
translations.idiomatic: In spring the consort went to the empress dowager's palace to pay her respects; as she was leaving, light like a dragon coiling appeared on the hem of her robe. The empress dowager asked about it, learned she was pregnant, and said to those near at hand, "When I was pregnant with the emperor there was truly this auspicious sign; now the consort has it too—her child will surely receive great fortune."

sentences.zh: 三月戊申，聖祖生。

translations.literal: In the third month on wushen day Shengzu was born.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on wushen day, Shengzu was born.

sentences.zh: 聖祖即位，尊為皇太后。

translations.literal: When Shengzu acceded to the throne, she was honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Shengzu acceded to the throne, she was honored as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年二月庚戌，崩，年二十四。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Kangxi, on gengxu day, she died, aged twenty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Kangxi 2, on gengxu day, she died, aged twenty-four.

sentences.zh: 初上徽號曰慈和皇太后。

translations.literal: When first granted an honorific title she was styled Empress Dowager Cihe.
translations.idiomatic: When first granted an honorific title she was styled Empress Dowager Cihe.

sentences.zh: 及崩，葬孝陵，上諡。

translations.literal: When she died she was buried at the Xiaoling Mausoleum, and the sovereign granted a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: After her death she was buried at the Xiaoling Mausoleum, and the emperor granted a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 雍正、乾隆累加諡，曰孝康慈和莊懿恭惠溫穆端靖崇天育聖章皇后。

translations.literal: Under Yongzheng and Qianlong additional posthumous honorifics were repeatedly added, so that she was called Empress Xiaokang Cihe Zhuangyi Gonghui Wenmu Duanjing Chongtian Yusheng Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzheng and Qianlong added further posthumous honorifics until she was styled Empress Xiaokang Cihe Zhuangyi Gonghui Wenmu Duanjing Chongtian Yusheng Zhang.

sentences.zh: 后家佟氏，本漢軍，上命改佟佳氏，入滿洲。

translations.literal: The empress's clan, the Tong clan, had originally been Han Banner; the sovereign ordered that they be changed to the Tunggiya clan and enrolled in the Manchu banners.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's clan, the Tong clan, had originally been Han Banner; the emperor ordered that they be changed to the Tunggiya clan and enrolled in the Manchu banners.

sentences.zh: 后族擡旗自此始。

translations.literal: The elevation of an empress's clan to a higher banner began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The practice of elevating an empress's clan to a higher banner began with her.

sentences.zh: 子一，聖祖。

translations.literal: Sons, one: Shengzu.
translations.idiomatic: She bore one son, Shengzu.

sentences.zh: 孝獻皇后，董鄂氏，內大臣鄂碩女。

translations.literal: Empress Xiaoxian, of the Donggo clan, was the daughter of Inner Minister Eshu.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaoxian, of the Donggo clan, was the daughter of Inner Minister Eshu.

sentences.zh: 年十八入侍，上眷之特厚，寵冠後宮。

translations.literal: At eighteen she entered service; the sovereign favored her with exceptional depth, and her favor surpassed all in the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen she entered service; the emperor favored her above all others, and her favor surpassed every woman in the rear palace.

sentences.zh: 順治十三年八月，立為賢妃。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Shunzhi, in the eighth month she was established as Worthy Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Shunzhi, in the eighth month she was made Worthy Consort.

sentences.zh: 十二月，進皇貴妃，行冊立禮，頒赦。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month she was advanced to Grand Imperial Noble Consort; the investiture rites were performed and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month she was advanced to Grand Imperial Noble Consort; the investiture rites were performed and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 上皇太后徽號，鄂碩本以軍功授一等精奇尼哈番，進三等伯。

translations.literal: When the sovereign granted the empress dowager an honorific title, Eshu, who had originally been granted a first-rank jingqi nihaan for military merit, was advanced to a third-rank earl.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor granted the empress dowager an honorific title, Eshu, who had originally been granted a first-rank jingqi nihaan for military merit, was advanced to a third-rank earl.

sentences.zh: 十七年八月，薨，上輟朝五日。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the seventeenth year she died; the sovereign suspended court for five days.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the seventeenth year she died; the emperor suspended court for five days.

sentences.zh: 追諡孝獻莊和至德宣仁溫惠端敬皇后。

translations.literal: She was posthumously titled Empress Xiaoxian Zhuanghe Zhide Xuanren Wenhui Duanjing.
translations.idiomatic: She was posthumously titled Empress Xiaoxian Zhuanghe Zhide Xuanren Wenhui Duanjing.

sentences.zh: 上親製行狀，略曰：「后婗靜循禮，事皇太后，奉養甚至，左右趨走，皇太后安之。

translations.literal: The sovereign personally composed a biographical account, which in summary says: "The empress was gentle, quiet, and observant of ritual; in serving the empress dowager she attended and nourished her with utmost devotion, hastening to her side at every turn, and the empress dowager was at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally composed a biographical account, which in summary says: "The empress was gentle, quiet, and observant of ritual; in serving the empress dowager she attended her with utmost devotion, ever at her side, and the empress dowager was at ease.

sentences.zh: 事朕，晨夕候興居，視飲食服御，曲體罔不悉。

translations.literal: In serving me she attended morning and evening to my rising and resting, watched over my food, drink, and apparel, and in every detail left nothing unattended.
translations.idiomatic: In serving me she attended morning and evening to my rising and resting, watched over my food, drink, and apparel, and left no detail unattended.

sentences.zh: 朕返蹕晏，必迎問寒暑，意少𠙏，則曰：『陛下歸晚，體得毋倦耶？』

translations.literal: When I returned late from the road she always came to ask after the cold or heat; if I seemed slightly weary she would say, 'Your Majesty returned late—are you not tired?'
translations.idiomatic: When I returned late from the road she always came to ask after the cold or heat; if I seemed slightly weary she would say, 'Your Majesty returned late—are you not tired?'

sentences.zh: 趣具餐，躬進之，命共餐，則辭。

translations.literal: She would hasten to prepare a meal and personally serve it; when ordered to dine together she would decline.
translations.idiomatic: She would hasten to prepare a meal and serve it herself; when ordered to dine together she would decline.

sentences.zh: 朕值慶典，舉數觴，必誡侍者，室無過燠，中夜罝罝起視。

translations.literal: When I attended a celebration and drank several cups she always admonished the attendants that the room must not be too warm, and at midnight she would rise again and again to look in on me.
translations.idiomatic: When I attended a celebration and drank several cups she always admonished the attendants that the room must not be too warm, and at midnight she would rise again and again to look in on me.

sentences.zh: 朕省封事，夜分，未嘗不侍側。

translations.literal: When I reviewed sealed memorials late into the night she never failed to attend at my side.
translations.idiomatic: When I reviewed sealed memorials late into the night she never failed to stay at my side.

sentences.zh: 諸曹循例章報，朕輒置之，后曰：『此雖奉行成法，安知無當更張，或有他故？

translations.literal: When the various offices submitted routine reports according to precedent I would set them aside; the empress would say, 'Though these follow established regulations, how can one know that nothing needs revision, or that there is no other cause?
translations.idiomatic: When the various offices submitted routine reports according to precedent I would set them aside; the empress would say, 'Though these follow established regulations, how can one know that nothing needs revision, or that there is no other cause?

sentences.zh: 奈何忽之！』

translations.literal: How can you neglect them!'
translations.idiomatic: How can you neglect them!'

sentences.zh: 令同閱，起謝：『不敢干政。』

translations.literal: She would have me review them together, then rise and apologize: 'I dare not interfere in governance.'
translations.idiomatic: She would have me review them together, then rise and apologize: 'I dare not interfere in governance.'

sentences.zh: 覽廷讞疏，握筆未忍下，后問是疏安所云，朕諭之，則泣曰：『諸辟皆愚無知，豈盡無冤？

translations.literal: When I reviewed court verdict memorials and held the brush unable to bring myself to sign, the empress would ask what the memorial concerned; when I explained it to her she would weep and say, 'Those condemned are all foolish and ignorant—can none of them be wrongfully accused?
translations.idiomatic: When I reviewed court verdict memorials and held the brush, unable to bring myself to sign, the empress would ask what the memorial concerned; when I explained it she would weep and say, 'Those condemned are all foolish and ignorant—can none of them be wrongfully accused?

sentences.zh: 宜求可矜宥者全活之！』

translations.literal: You should seek out those who may be pitied and spared and preserve their lives!'
translations.idiomatic: You should seek out those who may be pitied and spared and preserve their lives!'

sentences.zh: 大臣偶得罪，朕或不樂，后輒請霽威詳察。

translations.literal: When a minister occasionally gave offense and I was displeased, the empress would always ask that I clear my wrath and examine the matter carefully.
translations.idiomatic: When a minister occasionally gave offense and I was displeased, the empress would always ask that I clear my wrath and examine the matter carefully.

sentences.zh: 朕偶免朝，則諫毋倦勤。

translations.literal: When I occasionally excused myself from court she would remonstrate that I must not weary of diligence.
translations.idiomatic: When I occasionally excused myself from court she would remonstrate that I must not weary of diligence.

sentences.zh: 日講後，與言章句大義，輒喜。

translations.literal: After the daily lecture, when I discussed with her the larger meaning of the passages she would always rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: After the daily lecture, when I discussed with her the larger meaning of the passages she would always rejoice.

sentences.zh: 偶遺忘，則諫：『當服膺默識。』

translations.literal: When I occasionally forgot, she would remonstrate: 'You should take it to heart and commit it to silent memory.'
translations.idiomatic: When I occasionally forgot, she would remonstrate: 'You should take it to heart and commit it to silent memory.'

sentences.zh: 蒐狩，親騎射，則諫：『毋以萬邦仰庇之身，輕於馳驟。』

translations.literal: When hunting, if I personally rode and shot, she would remonstrate: 'Do not take the body on which all ten thousand states rely for shelter and lightly expose it to galloping and racing.'
translations.idiomatic: When I went hunting and rode and shot myself, she would remonstrate: 'Do not lightly expose the body on which all the realm relies for shelter to galloping and racing.'

sentences.zh: 偶有未稱旨，朕或加譙讓，始猶自明無過；

translations.literal: When something occasionally did not meet my pleasure, I might add reproof and blame; at first she would still clarify that she had done no wrong;
translations.idiomatic: When something occasionally displeased me, I might reprove and blame her; at first she would still insist she had done nothing wrong;

sentences.zh: 及聞姜后脫簪事，即有宜辯者，但引咎自責而已。

translations.literal: After hearing of Empress Jiang's removing-her-hairpin affair, even when there were matters that called for defense, she would only take blame upon herself.
translations.idiomatic: After she heard of Empress Jiang's removing-her-hairpin affair, even when there were matters that called for defense, she would only take blame upon herself.

sentences.zh: 后至節儉，不用金玉。

translations.literal: The empress was extremely frugal and did not use gold or jade.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was extremely frugal and did not use gold or jade.

sentences.zh: 誦四書及易已卒業；

translations.literal: She had completed recitation of the Four Books and the Changes;
translations.idiomatic: She had completed the Four Books and the Changes;

sentences.zh: 習書，未久即精。

translations.literal: In practicing calligraphy, before long she became skilled.
translations.idiomatic: In calligraphy, before long she became accomplished.

sentences.zh: 朕喻以禪學，參究若有所省。

translations.literal: When I instructed her in Chan Buddhism and she investigated together with me, she seemed to gain some insight.
translations.idiomatic: When I taught her Chan Buddhism and she studied it with me, she seemed to gain some insight.

sentences.zh: 后初病，皇太后使問安否，必對曰：『安。』

translations.literal: When the empress first fell ill, the empress dowager sent someone to ask after her health; she always replied: 'Well.'
translations.idiomatic: When the empress first fell ill, the empress dowager sent someone to ask after her health; she always replied: 'Well.'

sentences.zh: 疾甚，朕及今后、諸妃、嬪環視之，后曰：『吾殆將不起，此中澄定，亦無所苦，獨不及酬皇太后暨陛下恩萬一。

translations.literal: When the illness grew severe, I together with the present empress, the various consorts and ladies-in-waiting gathered around to look upon her; the empress said: 'I fear I shall not rise again; within I am clear and settled and feel no suffering; only that I cannot repay even one ten-thousandth of the empress dowager's and Your Majesty's grace.
translations.idiomatic: When the illness grew severe, I together with the present empress, the various consorts and ladies-in-waiting gathered around her; the empress said: 'I fear I shall not rise again; within I am clear and at peace and feel no pain; only that I cannot repay even one ten-thousandth of the empress dowager's and Your Majesty's grace.

sentences.zh: 妾歿，陛下宜自愛！

translations.literal: When your humble servant dies, Your Majesty should take care of yourself!
translations.idiomatic: When I am gone, Your Majesty should take care of yourself!

sentences.zh: 惟皇太后必傷悼，奈何？』

translations.literal: Only the empress dowager will surely grieve deeply—what is to be done?'
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager will surely grieve deeply—what is to be done?'

sentences.zh: 既又令以諸王賻施貧乏，復屬左右毋以珍麗物斂。

translations.literal: She then also ordered that the funeral gifts from the princes be distributed to the poor, and again charged those near her not to bury her with precious and fine objects.
translations.idiomatic: She then also ordered that the funeral gifts from the princes be given to the poor, and again charged those near her not to bury her with precious and fine objects.

sentences.zh: 歿後，皇太后哀之甚。」

translations.literal: After her death the empress dowager grieved for her exceedingly."
translations.idiomatic: After her death the empress dowager grieved for her deeply."

sentences.zh: 行狀數千言，又命大學士金之俊別作傳。

translations.literal: The biographical account ran to several thousand characters, and he also ordered Grand Secretary Jin Zhijun to write a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: The biographical account ran to several thousand characters, and he also ordered Grand Secretary Jin Zhijun to write a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 是歲，命秋讞停決，從后志也。

translations.literal: That year he ordered that autumn criminal verdicts be suspended, in accordance with the empress's wish.
translations.idiomatic: That year he ordered that autumn criminal verdicts be suspended, in accordance with the empress's wish.

sentences.zh: 時鄂碩已前卒，后世父羅碩，授一等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: By that time Eshu had already died earlier; the empress's great-uncle Luoshuo was granted a first-rank ashan i haan.
translations.idiomatic: By then Eshu had already died; the empress's great-uncle Luoshuo was granted a first-rank ashan i haan.

sentences.zh: 及上崩，遺詔以后喪祭逾禮為罪己之一，

translations.literal: When the sovereign died, his testamentary edict listed excessive mourning sacrifices for the empress as one of his self-reproaches.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, his testamentary edict listed excessive mourning sacrifices for the empress as one of his self-reproaches.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年，合葬孝陵，主不祔廟，歲時配食饗殿。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi, she was buried together at the Xiaoling Mausoleum; her tablet was not enshrined in the ancestral temple; at the seasonal sacrifices she received offerings in the Hall of Communal Feasting.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kangxi, she was buried together at the Xiaoling Mausoleum; her tablet was not enshrined in the ancestral temple; at the seasonal sacrifices she received offerings in the Hall of Communal Feasting.

sentences.zh: 子一，生三月而殤，未命名。

translations.literal: Sons, one: died in infancy at three months, never given a name.
translations.idiomatic: She bore one son, who died in infancy at three months and was never given a name.

sentences.zh: 貞妃，棟鄂氏，一等阿達哈哈番巴度女。

translations.literal: Consort Zhen, of the Donggo clan, was the daughter of Badu, a first-rank adaha haan.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Zhen, of the Donggo clan, was the daughter of Badu, a first-rank adaha haan.

sentences.zh: 殉世祖。

translations.literal: She followed Shizu in death.
translations.idiomatic: She followed Shizu in death.

sentences.zh: 聖祖追封為皇考貞妃。

translations.literal: Shengzu posthumously enfeoffed her as Imperial Father's Consort Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Shengzu posthumously enfeoffed her as Imperial Father's Consort Zhen.

sentences.zh: 淑惠妃，博爾濟吉特氏，孝惠皇后妹也，

translations.literal: Imperial Consort Shuhui, of the Borjigit clan, was a younger sister of Empress Xiaohui.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Consort Shuhui, of the Borjigit clan, was a younger sister of Empress Xiaohui.

sentences.zh: 冊為妃，

translations.literal: She was invested as consort.
translations.idiomatic: She was invested as consort.

sentences.zh: 尊封皇考淑惠妃。

translations.literal: She was honored as Imperial Father's Imperial Consort Shuhui.
translations.idiomatic: She was honored as Imperial Father's Imperial Consort Shuhui.

sentences.zh: 妃最老壽，以五十二年十月薨。

translations.literal: The consort lived longest of all, dying in the tenth month of the fifty-second year.
translations.idiomatic: She lived longer than any of the others, dying in the tenth month of the fifty-second year.

sentences.zh: 同時尊封者：浩齊特博爾濟吉特氏為恭靖妃，阿霸垓博爾濟吉特氏為端順妃，皆無所出；

translations.literal: Those honored at the same time: Haqit Borjigit was made Imperial Consort Gongjing, Abagai Borjigit was made Imperial Consort Duanshun—both bore no children;
translations.idiomatic: Those honored at the same time were Haqit Borjigit as Imperial Consort Gongjing and Abagai Borjigit as Imperial Consort Duanshun—neither bore children;

sentences.zh: 棟鄂氏為寧慤妃，在世祖時號庶妃，子一，福全。

translations.literal: The Donggo clan woman was made Imperial Consort Ningque; during Shizu's reign she was called a lesser consort; one son: Fuquan.
translations.idiomatic: The Donggo woman was made Imperial Consort Ningque; during Shizu's reign she was called a lesser consort; she bore one son, Fuquan.

sentences.zh: 又恪妃，石氏，灤州人，吏部侍郎申女。

translations.literal: Also Imperial Consort Ke, née Shi, a native of Luanzhou, daughter of Vice Minister of the Board of Civil Office Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Also Imperial Consort Ke, née Shi, a native of Luanzhou, daughter of Vice Minister Shen of the Board of Civil Office.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘗選漢官女備六宮，妃與焉。

translations.literal: Shizu once selected daughters of Han officials to fill the six palaces; the consort was among them.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu once selected daughters of Han officials to fill the six palaces; the consort was among them.

sentences.zh: 居永壽宮。

translations.literal: She resided in the Yongshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: She resided in the Yongshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年薨，聖祖追封皇考恪妃。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi, when she died, Shengzu posthumously enfeoffed her as Imperial Father's Imperial Consort Ke.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Kangxi, when she died, Shengzu posthumously enfeoffed her as Imperial Father's Imperial Consort Ke.

sentences.zh: 又在三妃前，世祖庶妃有子女者，又有八人：*穆克圖氏，子永幹，八歲殤；

translations.literal: Also, before these three consorts, among Shizu's lesser consorts who had children, there were eight more: *Muketu clan, son Yonggan, died in infancy at eight;
translations.idiomatic: Also, before these three consorts, among Shizu's lesser consorts who had children, there were eight more: Muketu clan, son Yonggan, died in infancy at eight;

sentences.zh: *巴氏，子鈕鈕，為世祖長子，二歲殤，女二，一六歲殤，一七歲殤；

translations.literal: *Ba clan, son Niuniu, Shizu's eldest son, died in infancy at two; two daughters, one died at six, one at seven;
translations.idiomatic: Ba clan, son Niuniu, Shizu's eldest son, died in infancy at two; two daughters, one died at six and one at seven;

sentences.zh: *陳氏，子一，常寧；

translations.literal: *Chen clan, one son: Changning;
translations.idiomatic: Chen clan, one son, Changning;

sentences.zh: *唐氏，子一，奇授，七歲殤；

translations.literal: *Tang clan, one son: Qishou, died in infancy at seven;
translations.idiomatic: Tang clan, one son, Qishou, died in infancy at seven;

sentences.zh: *鈕氏，子一，隆禧；

translations.literal: *Niohuru clan, one son: Longxi;
translations.idiomatic: Niohuru clan, one son, Longxi;

sentences.zh: *楊氏，女一，下嫁納爾杜；

translations.literal: *Yang clan, one daughter who married downward to Naerdu;
translations.idiomatic: Yang clan, one daughter who married Naerdu;

sentences.zh: *烏蘇氏，女一，八歲殤；

translations.literal: *Usu clan, one daughter, died in infancy at eight;
translations.idiomatic: Usu clan, one daughter, died in infancy at eight;

sentences.zh: *納喇氏，女一，五歲殤。

translations.literal: *Nara clan, one daughter, died in infancy at five.
translations.idiomatic: Nara clan, one daughter, died in infancy at five.

sentences.zh: 孝誠仁皇后，赫舍里氏，輔政大臣、一等大臣索尼孫，領侍衛內大臣噶布喇女。

translations.literal: Empress Xiaocheng Ren, of the Heseri clan, was the daughter of Grand Secretary of the Interior Gabul'a, grandson of the regent minister and first-rank minister Suoni.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaocheng Ren, of the Heseri clan, was the daughter of Grand Secretary of the Interior Gabul'a, grandson of the regent minister and first-rank minister Suoni.

sentences.zh: 康熙四年七月，冊為皇后。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kangxi, in the seventh month she was invested as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kangxi, in the seventh month she was invested as empress.

sentences.zh: 十三年五月丙寅，生皇二子允礽，即於是日崩，年二十二。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, fifth month bingyin day, she bore the second imperial son Yunreng, and on that same day died, aged twenty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, on bingyin day in the fifth month, she bore the second imperial son Yunreng, and died that same day, aged twenty-two.

sentences.zh: 諡曰仁孝皇后。

translations.literal: She was posthumously titled Empress Renxiao.
translations.idiomatic: She was posthumously titled Empress Renxiao.

sentences.zh: 二十年，葬孝東陵之東，即景陵也，

translations.literal: In the twentieth year she was buried east of the Xiaodong Mausoleum, which is the Jing Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year she was buried east of the Xiaodong Mausoleum, at what is called the Jing Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，改諡。

translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaojing Xian of Shizong, of the Ula Nara clan, was the daughter of Grand Secretary Feiyanggu.

sentences.zh: 世宗為皇子，聖祖冊后為嫡福晉，

translations.literal: When Shizong was a prince, Shengzu invested the empress as primary consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong was a prince, Shengzu invested her as primary consort.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，冊為皇后。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, she was invested as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongzheng, when he acceded, she was invested as empress.

sentences.zh: 九年九月己丑，崩。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, ninth month, on jichou day, she died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, ninth month, on jichou day, she died.

sentences.zh: 時上病初癒，欲親臨含斂，諸大臣諫止。

translations.literal: At the time the sovereign had just recovered from illness and wished to attend the laying-in-state in person; the ministers remonstrated and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had just recovered from illness and wished to attend the laying-in-state in person, but the ministers remonstrated and stopped him.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「皇后自垂髫之年，奉皇考命，作配朕躬。

translations.literal: The sovereign issued an edict saying: "Since the empress was a child, by Imperial Father's command she was joined to me as consort.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict saying: "Since the empress was a child, by my father's command she was joined to me as consort.

sentences.zh: 結褵以來，四十餘載，孝順恭敬，始終一致。

translations.literal: Since our marriage more than forty years ago, she has been filial, obedient, and reverent, consistent from first to last.
translations.idiomatic: Since our marriage more than forty years ago, she has been filial, obedient, and reverent, consistent from first to last.

sentences.zh: 朕調理經年，今始全愈，若親臨喪次，觸景增悲，非攝養所宜。

translations.literal: I have been convalescing for years and have only now fully recovered; if I personally attend the mourning hall, the sight will increase my grief, which is not suitable for my recuperation.
translations.idiomatic: I have been convalescing for years and have only now fully recovered; if I personally attend the mourning hall, the sight will increase my grief, which is not suitable for my recuperation.

sentences.zh: 但皇后喪事，國家典儀雖備，而朕禮數未周。

translations.literal: Yet in the empress's funeral, though the state's canonical rites are complete, my personal observances are not thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the empress's funeral, though the state's canonical rites are complete, my personal observances are not thorough.

sentences.zh: 權衡輕重，如何使情文兼盡，其具議以聞。」

translations.literal: Weigh what is light and heavy, and deliberate on how to fulfill both feeling and ritual completely; submit a detailed report."
translations.idiomatic: Weigh what is light and heavy, and deliberate on how to fulfill both feeling and ritual completely; submit a detailed report."

sentences.zh: 諸大臣議，以明會典皇后喪無親臨祭奠之禮，令皇子朝夕奠，遇祭，例可遣官，乞停親奠，從之。

translations.literal: The ministers deliberated that according to the Ming Statutes there was no ritual for the emperor to personally attend memorial offerings at an empress's funeral; princes should offer morning and evening libations; when sacrifices occurred, officials could be dispatched as precedent permitted; they begged that personal attendance be stopped; the sovereign assented.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers deliberated that according to the Ming Statutes there was no ritual for the emperor to personally attend memorial offerings at an empress's funeral; princes should offer morning and evening libations, and when sacrifices occurred officials could be dispatched as precedent permitted; they begged that personal attendance be stopped, and the emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 諡孝敬皇后。

translations.literal: Her posthumous title was Empress Xiaojing.
translations.idiomatic: She was posthumously titled Empress Xiaojing.

sentences.zh: 及世宗崩，合葬泰陵。

translations.literal: When Shizong died, she was buried together with him at the Tai Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong died, she was buried with him at the Tai Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 乾隆、嘉慶累加諡，曰孝敬恭和懿順昭惠莊肅安康佐天翊聖憲皇后。

translations.literal: Under Qianlong and Jiaqing additional posthumous honorifics were repeatedly added, so that she was called Empress Xiaojing Gonghe Yishun Zhaohui Zhuangsu Ankang Zuotian Yisheng Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlong and Jiaqing added further posthumous honorifics until she was styled Empress Xiaojing Gonghe Yishun Zhaohui Zhuangsu Ankang Zuotian Yisheng Xian.

sentences.zh: 孝聖憲皇后，鈕祜祿氏，四品典儀凌柱女。

translations.literal: Empress Xiaosheng Xian, of the Niohuru clan, was the daughter of Fourth-rank Dianyi Lingzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaosheng Xian, of the Niohuru clan, was the daughter of Fourth-rank Dianyi Lingzhu.

sentences.zh: 后年十三，事世宗潛邸，號格格。

translations.literal: At thirteen the empress attended Shizong's princely household and was styled gege.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen she attended Shizong's princely household and was styled gege.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十年八月庚午，高宗生。

translations.literal: In the 50 year of Kangxi, in the eighth month on gengwu day Gaozong was born.
translations.idiomatic: In the 50 year of Kangxi, in the eighth month, on gengwu day, Gaozong was born.

sentences.zh: 雍正中，封熹妃，進熹貴妃。

translations.literal: During Yongzheng she was enfeoffed as Consort Xi and advanced to Noble Consort Xi.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongzheng she was made Consort Xi and advanced to Noble Consort Xi.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，以世宗遺命，尊為皇太后，居慈寧宮。

translations.literal: When Gaozong acceded to the throne, by Shizong's testament she was honored as empress dowager and resided in the Cining Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong acceded to the throne, by Shizong's testament she was honored as empress dowager and resided in the Cining Palace.

sentences.zh: 高宗事太后孝，以天下養，惟亦兢兢守家法，重國體。

translations.literal: Gaozong was filial toward the empress dowager and provided for her with the wealth of the realm, yet he also carefully upheld household discipline and the dignity of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong was filial toward the empress dowager and provided for her with the wealth of the realm, yet he also carefully upheld household discipline and the dignity of the state.

sentences.zh: 太后偶言順天府東有廢寺當重修，上從之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager casually mentioned that east of Shuntian Prefecture there was an abandoned temple that should be restored; the sovereign agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager casually mentioned that east of Shuntian Prefecture there was an abandoned temple that should be restored, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 即召宮監，諭：「汝等嘗侍聖祖，幾曾見昭聖太后當日令聖祖修蓋廟宇？

translations.literal: He immediately summoned the palace eunuchs and instructed them: "You once attended Shengzu—when did you ever see Empress Dowager Zhaosheng in her day have Shengzu repair or build temples?
translations.idiomatic: He immediately summoned the palace eunuchs and instructed them: "You once attended Shengzu—when did you ever see Empress Dowager Zhaosheng in her day have Shengzu repair or build temples?

sentences.zh: 嗣後當奏止！」

translations.literal: Hereafter you must memorialize to stop it!"
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter you must memorialize to stop it!"

sentences.zh: 宮監引悟真庵尼入內，導太后弟入蒼震門謝恩，上屢誡之。

translations.literal: The palace eunuchs brought nuns from Wuzhen Nunnery into the palace and guided the empress dowager's younger brother through the Cangzhen Gate to offer thanks; the sovereign repeatedly admonished them.
translations.idiomatic: The palace eunuchs brought nuns from Wuzhen Nunnery into the palace and guided the empress dowager's younger brother through the Cangzhen Gate to offer thanks; the emperor repeatedly admonished them.

sentences.zh: 上每出巡幸，輒奉太后以行，南巡者三，東巡者三，幸五台山者三，幸中州者一。

translations.literal: Whenever the sovereign went on tour he always brought the empress dowager; southern tours three times, eastern tours three times, visits to Wutaishan three times, and a tour of the Central Plains once.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor went on tour he always brought the empress dowager along: three southern tours, three eastern tours, three visits to Wutaishan, and one tour of the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 謁孝陵，獮木蘭，歲必至焉。

translations.literal: Paying respects at the Xia Mausoleum and hunting at Mulan, he went every year without fail.
translations.idiomatic: Paying respects at the Xia Mausoleum and hunting at Mulan, he went every year without fail.

sentences.zh: 遇萬壽，率王大臣奉觴稱慶。

translations.literal: On her birthday celebrations he led princes and ministers to offer toasts and offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: On her birthday celebrations he led princes and ministers to offer toasts and offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 四十二年正月庚寅，崩，年八十六。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, first month, on gengyin day, she died, aged eighty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year, first month, on gengyin day, she died, aged eighty-six.

sentences.zh: 葬泰陵東北，曰泰東陵。

translations.literal: She was buried northeast of the Tai Mausoleum, called the Taidong Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: She was buried northeast of the Tai Mausoleum, called the Taidong Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 初尊太后，上徽號。

translations.literal: When she was first honored as empress dowager, an honorific title was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: When she was first honored as empress dowager, an honorific title was conferred.

sentences.zh: 國有慶，屢加上，曰崇德慈宣康惠敦和裕壽純禧恭懿安祺寧豫皇太后。

translations.literal: When the state had celebrations, additional honorifics were repeatedly added, so that she was called Empress Dowager Chongde Cixuan Kanghui Dunhe Yushou Chunxi Gongyi Anqi Ningyu.
translations.idiomatic: When the state had celebrations, additional honorifics were repeatedly added until she was styled Empress Dowager Chongde Cixuan Kanghui Dunhe Yushou Chunxi Gongyi Anqi Ningyu.

sentences.zh: 既葬，上諡。

translations.literal: After burial the sovereign granted a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: After burial the emperor granted a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶中，再加諡，曰孝聖慈宣康惠敦和誠徽仁穆敬天光聖憲皇后。

translations.literal: During Jiaqing additional posthumous honorifics were added, so that she was called Empress Xiaosheng Cixuan Kanghui Dunhe Chenghui Renmu Jingtian Guangsheng Xian.
translations.idiomatic: During Jiaqing further posthumous honorifics were added until she was styled Empress Xiaosheng Cixuan Kanghui Dunhe Chenghui Renmu Jingtian Guangsheng Xian.

translations.idiomatic: She bore one son, Gaozong.

translations.idiomatic: Imperial Noble Consort Dunsu, of the Nian clan, was the daughter of Governor Xialling.

translations.idiomatic: She attended Shizong's princely household as side primary consort.

translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongzheng, she was made Imperial Consort.

translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the third year, gravely ill, she was advanced to Imperial Noble Consort.

translations.idiomatic: It was also decreed that if her illness proved fatal, the funeral rites should follow the precedent for an imperial noble consort.

sentences.zh: 妃薨逾月，妃兄羹堯得罪死。

translations.literal: More than a month after the consort died, her elder brother Nian Gengyao was found guilty and executed.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month after she died, her elder brother Nian Gengyao was found guilty and executed.

sentences.zh: 諡曰敦肅皇貴妃。

translations.idiomatic: She was posthumously titled Imperial Noble Consort Dunsu.

translations.literal: Early in Qianlong she was buried with him at the Tai Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianlong she was buried with him at the Tai Mausoleum.

translations.idiomatic: She bore one daughter, who also died in infancy.

translations.idiomatic: Imperial Noble Consort Chunque, of the Geng clan.

translations.idiomatic: She attended Shizong's princely household as gege.

translations.literal: During Yongzheng she was enfeoffed as Lady Yu and advanced to Consort Yu.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongzheng she was made Lady Yu and advanced to Consort Yu.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，屢加尊為裕皇貴太妃，

translations.literal: During Gaozong's reign she was repeatedly honored as Grand Imperial Consort Yu.
translations.idiomatic: During Gaozong's reign she was repeatedly honored as Grand Imperial Consort Yu.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十九年，薨，年九十六。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year of Qianlong, she died, aged ninety-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year of Qianlong, she died, aged ninety-six.

sentences.zh: 諡曰純慤皇貴妃。

translations.literal: Her posthumous title was Imperial Noble Consort Chunque.
translations.idiomatic: She was posthumously titled Imperial Noble Consort Chunque.

sentences.zh: 葬妃園寢，位諸妃上。

translations.literal: She was buried in the consort garden tomb, placed above the other consorts.
translations.idiomatic: She was buried in the consort garden tomb, placed above the other consorts.

translations.literal: Sons, one: Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: She bore one son, Hongzhou.

translations.idiomatic: Shizong's consorts also included: Consort Qi, of the Li clan.

translations.idiomatic: She bore three sons: Hongpan and Hongyun, both of whom died in infancy;

translations.idiomatic: Consort Qian, of the Liu clan.

translations.idiomatic: Gaozong honored her as Imperial Father's Consort Qian.

translations.literal: Empress Xiaoxian Chun of Gaozong, of the Fuca clan, was the daughter of Chahar Commander Li Rongbao.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaoxian Chun of Gaozong, of the Fuca clan, was the daughter of Chahar Commander Li Rongbao.

sentences.zh: 高宗為皇子，，世宗冊后為嫡福晉，

translations.literal: When Gaozong was a prince, Shizong invested the empress as primary consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong was a prince, Shizong invested her as primary consort.

sentences.zh: 冊為皇后。

translations.literal: She was invested as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When he acceded, she was invested as empress.

sentences.zh: 后恭儉，平居以通草絨花為飾，不御珠翠。

translations.literal: The empress was respectful and frugal; in daily life she adorned herself with tongcao velvet flowers and did not wear pearls or kingfisher feathers.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was respectful and frugal; in daily life she adorned herself with tongcao velvet flowers and did not wear pearls or kingfisher feathers.

sentences.zh: 歲時以鹿羔沴毧制為荷包進上，仿先世關外遺制，示不忘本也。

translations.literal: At New Year she made pouches from deerskin and down for the sovereign, imitating the old customs beyond the pass to show she did not forget her origins.
translations.idiomatic: At New Year she made pouches from deerskin and down for the emperor, imitating the old customs beyond the pass to show she did not forget her origins.

sentences.zh: 上甚重之。

translations.literal: The sovereign greatly valued this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor greatly valued this.

sentences.zh: 十三年，從上東巡，還蹕，三月乙未，后崩於德州舟次，年三十七。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, accompanying the sovereign on an eastern tour, on the return journey, third month on yiwei day, the empress died aboard ship at Dezhou, aged thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, accompanying the emperor on an eastern tour, on the return journey, third month on yiwei day, the empress died aboard ship at Dezhou, aged thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 上深慟，兼程還京師，殯於長春宮，服縞素十二日。

translations.literal: The sovereign grieved deeply, hurried back to the capital by forced marches, laid her in state at the Changchun Palace, and wore unhemmed white mourning for twelve days.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved deeply, hurried back to the capital by forced marches, laid her in state at the Changchun Palace, and wore unhemmed white mourning for twelve days.

sentences.zh: 初，皇貴妃高佳氏薨，上諡以慧賢，后在側，曰：「吾他日期以「孝賢」，可乎？」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Imperial Noble Consort Gao died, the sovereign granted the posthumous epithet Huixian; the empress was at his side and said, "When my time comes, might you style me Xiaoxian?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Imperial Noble Consort Gao died, the emperor granted the posthumous epithet Huixian; the empress was at his side and said, "When my time comes, might you style me Xiaoxian?"

sentences.zh: 至是，上遂用為諡。

translations.literal: Now the sovereign adopted it as her posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: Now the emperor adopted it as her posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 並製《述悲賦》，曰：「《易》何以首乾坤？

translations.literal: He also composed the "Lamentation of Grief," which says: "Why does the Changes begin with Qian and Kun?
translations.idiomatic: He also composed the "Lamentation of Grief," which says: "Why does the Changes begin with Qian and Kun?

sentences.zh: 《詩》何以首《關睢》？

translations.literal: Why does the Poetry begin with 'Guanju'?
translations.idiomatic: Why does the Poetry begin with 'Guanju'?

sentences.zh: 惟人倫之伊始，固天儷之與齊。

translations.literal: Only at the outset of human relations are heaven's paired partners joined as one.
translations.idiomatic: Only at the outset of human relations are heaven's paired partners joined as one.

sentences.zh: 念懿后之作配，廿二年而於斯。

translations.literal: Remembering when the worthy empress became my consort—twenty-two years have passed to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering when the worthy empress became my consort—twenty-two years have passed to this day.

sentences.zh: 痛一旦之永訣，隔陰陽而莫知。

translations.literal: I grieve that in one morning she parted forever, divided by yin and yang with no knowledge of each other.
translations.idiomatic: I grieve that in one morning she parted forever, divided by yin and yang with no knowledge of each other.

sentences.zh: 昔皇考之命偶，用掄德於名門。

translations.literal: Of old Imperial Father commanded my marriage, selecting virtue from a distinguished clan.
translations.idiomatic: Of old my father commanded my marriage, selecting virtue from a distinguished clan.

sentences.zh: 俾逑予而屍藻，定嘉禮於渭濱。

translations.literal: He gave her to me to serve at the ancestral altar and established the auspicious rites on the Wei riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: He gave her to me to serve at the ancestral altar and established the auspicious rites on the Wei riverbank.

sentences.zh: 在青宮而養德，即治壺而淑身。

translations.literal: In the eastern palace she cultivated virtue and governed the inner household with modest conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In the eastern palace she cultivated virtue and governed the inner household with modest conduct.

sentences.zh: 縱糟糠之未歷，實同甘而共辛。

translations.literal: Though we had not yet shared coarse fare, we truly shared sweetness and bitterness alike.
translations.idiomatic: Though we had not yet shared coarse fare, we truly shared sweetness and bitterness alike.

sentences.zh: 乃其正位坤寧，克贊乾清。

translations.literal: Then she took her place in the Kun Ning Palace and helped uphold the Qian Qing Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Then she took her place in the Kun Ning Palace and helped uphold the Qian Qing Hall.

sentences.zh: 奉慈闈之溫凊，為九卿之儀型。

translations.literal: She attended the empress dowager with warm care in winter and cool in summer, and was a model for the nine ministers.
translations.idiomatic: She attended the empress dowager with warm care in winter and cool in summer, and was a model for the nine ministers.

sentences.zh: 克儉於家，爰始繅品而育繭；

translations.literal: Frugal in the household, she began by reeling silk and raising silkworms;
translations.idiomatic: Frugal in the household, she began by reeling silk and raising silkworms;

sentences.zh: 克勤於邦，亦知較雨而課晴。

translations.literal: diligent in state affairs, she also concerned herself with comparing rainfall and assessing clear skies.
translations.idiomatic: diligent in state affairs, she also concerned herself with comparing rainfall and assessing clear skies.

sentences.zh: 嗟予命之不辰兮，痛元嫡之連棄。

translations.literal: Alas that my fate is ill-starred—I mourn that my sons by the primary consort were taken one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Alas that my fate is ill-starred—I mourn that my sons by the primary consort were taken one after another.

sentences.zh: 致黯然以內傷兮，遂邈爾而長逝。

translations.literal: This inward sorrow leaves me wan, and she has passed far away.
translations.idiomatic: This inward sorrow leaves me wan, and she has passed far away.

sentences.zh: 撫諸子如一出兮，豈彼此之分視？

translations.literal: She treated all the sons as one—how could she have regarded them with partiality?
translations.idiomatic: She treated all the sons as one—how could she have regarded them with partiality?

sentences.zh: 值乖舛之疊遘兮，誰不增夫怨懟？

translations.literal: When misfortune piled upon misfortune, who did not increase in resentment?
translations.idiomatic: When misfortune piled upon misfortune, who did not increase in resentment?

sentences.zh: 況顧予之傷悼兮，更怳悢而切意。

translations.literal: Yet when she saw my grief, she grew only more anxious and tender toward me.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when she saw my grief, she grew only more anxious and tender toward me.

sentences.zh: 尚強歡以相慰兮，每禁情而制淚。

translations.literal: She still forced herself to console me, each time restraining emotion and holding back tears.
translations.idiomatic: She still forced herself to console me, each time restraining emotion and holding back tears.

sentences.zh: 制淚兮淚滴襟，強歡兮歡匪心。

translations.literal: Restraining tears—tears soaking my collar; forcing joy—joy that was not from the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Restraining tears—tears soaking my collar; forcing joy—joy that was not from the heart.

sentences.zh: 聿當春而啟轡，隨予駕以東臨。

translations.literal: Just as spring opened the reins, she followed my carriage eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Just as spring opened the reins, she followed my carriage eastward.

sentences.zh: 抱輕疾兮念衆勞，促歸程兮變故遭。

translations.literal: Bearing a slight illness, mindful of the labor of the multitude, she urged a quick return—and sudden calamity befell.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing a slight illness, mindful of the labor of the multitude, she urged a quick return—and sudden calamity befell.

sentences.zh: 登畫舫兮陳翟褕，由潞河兮還內朝。

translations.literal: Boarding the painted barge draped in red, by the Lu River we returned to the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: Boarding the painted barge draped in red, by the Lu River we returned to the inner court.

sentences.zh: 去內朝兮時未幾，致邂逅兮怨無已。

translations.literal: Leaving the inner court, little time had passed before we encountered this bitter parting with unending grief.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving the inner court, little time had passed before we encountered this bitter parting with unending grief.

sentences.zh: 切自尤兮不可追，論生平兮定於此。

translations.literal: I can only blame myself—it cannot be undone; our life together is fixed at this.
translations.idiomatic: I can only blame myself—it cannot be undone; our life together is fixed at this.

sentences.zh: 影與形兮難去一，居忽忽兮如有失。

translations.literal: Shadow and form can scarcely be separated; living in a daze as though something were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Shadow and form can scarcely be separated; living in a daze as though something were lost.

sentences.zh: 對嬪嬙兮想芳型，顧和敬兮憐弱質。

translations.literal: Facing the palace ladies I recall her graceful bearing; looking on Hejing I pity her delicate nature.
translations.idiomatic: Facing the palace ladies I recall her graceful bearing; looking on Hejing I pity her delicate nature.

sentences.zh: 望湘浦兮何先徂，求北海兮乏神術。

translations.literal: Gazing toward the Xiang River—who has departed first? Seeking the North Sea—I lack divine skill.
translations.idiomatic: Gazing toward the Xiang River—who has departed first? Seeking the North Sea—I lack divine skill.

sentences.zh: 循喪儀兮愴徒然，例展禽兮諡孝賢。

translations.literal: Following mourning rites only deepens sorrow in vain; following precedent for Zhanqin, the posthumous title is Xiaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: Following mourning rites only deepens sorrow in vain; following precedent for Zhanqin, the posthumous title is Xiaoxian.

sentences.zh: 思遺徽之莫盡兮，詎兩字之能宣。

translations.literal: Thinking that her remaining virtue cannot be exhausted—how can two characters suffice to proclaim it?
translations.idiomatic: Thinking that her remaining virtue cannot be exhausted—how can two characters suffice to proclaim it?

sentences.zh: 包四德而首出兮，謂庶幾其可傳。

translations.literal: Embracing the four virtues and standing foremost—I thought this could be passed down.
translations.idiomatic: Embracing the four virtues and standing foremost—I thought this could be passed down.

sentences.zh: 驚時序之代謝兮，屆十旬而迅如。

translations.literal: Startled by the seasons' succession—ten days pass swift as this.
translations.idiomatic: Startled by the seasons' succession—ten days pass swift as this.

sentences.zh: 覩新昌而增慟兮，陳舊物而憶初。

translations.literal: Seeing the new hall adds to my grief; placing out old things recalls the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the new hall adds to my grief; placing out old things recalls the beginning.

sentences.zh: 亦有時而暫弭兮，旋觸緒而欷歔。

translations.literal: Sometimes grief is briefly stilled, but at once touching the thread of memory brings sobs.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes grief is briefly stilled, but at once touching the thread of memory brings sobs.

sentences.zh: 信人生之如夢兮，了萬事之皆虛。

translations.literal: Truly human life is like a dream—all ten thousand affairs are empty.
translations.idiomatic: Truly human life is like a dream—all ten thousand affairs are empty.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，悲莫悲兮生別離，失內位兮孰予隨？

translations.literal: Alas, nothing is more sorrowful than parting in life; losing the inner consort—who will follow me?
translations.idiomatic: Alas, nothing is more sorrowful than parting in life; losing the inner consort—who will follow me?

sentences.zh: 入淑房兮闃寂，披鳳幄兮空垂。

translations.literal: Entering the quiet inner chamber, parting the phoenix canopy—it hangs empty.
translations.idiomatic: Entering the quiet inner chamber, parting the phoenix canopy—it hangs empty.

sentences.zh: 春風秋月兮盡於此已，夏日冬夜兮知復何時？」

translations.literal: Spring wind and autumn moon—all end here; summer days and winter nights—when will they come again?"
translations.idiomatic: Spring wind and autumn moon—all end here; summer days and winter nights—when will they come again?"

sentences.zh: 十七年，葬孝陵西勝水峪，後即於此起裕陵焉。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year she was buried at Shengshui Valley west of the Xiao Mausoleum; afterward the Yu Mausoleum was built there.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year she was buried at Shengshui Valley west of the Xiao Mausoleum; afterward the Yu Mausoleum was built there.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶、道光累加諡，曰孝賢誠正敦穆仁惠徽恭康順輔天昌聖純皇后。

translations.literal: Under Jiaqing and Daoguang additional posthumous honorifics were repeatedly added, so that she was called Empress Xiaoxian Chengzheng Dunmu Renhui Huigong Kangshun Futian Changsheng Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaqing and Daoguang added further posthumous honorifics until she was styled Empress Xiaoxian Chengzheng Dunmu Renhui Huigong Kangshun Futian Changsheng Chun.

sentences.zh: 子二：永璉、永琮。

translations.literal: Sons, two: Yonglian and Yongcong.
translations.idiomatic: She bore two sons: Yonglian and Yongcong.

sentences.zh: 女二：一殤，一下嫁色布騰巴爾珠爾。

translations.literal: Daughters, two: one died in infancy; one married downward to Sebutengba'erzhu'er.
translations.idiomatic: She bore two daughters: one died in infancy; one married Sebutengba'erzhu'er.

sentences.zh: 皇后，烏喇那拉氏，佐領那爾布女。

translations.literal: The empress, of the Ula Nara clan, was the daughter of Banner Captain Na'erbu.
translations.idiomatic: The empress, of the Ula Nara clan, was the daughter of Banner Captain Na'erbu.

sentences.zh: 后事高宗潛邸，為側室福晉，

translations.literal: The empress attended Gaozong's princely household as side chamber primary consort.
translations.idiomatic: She attended Gaozong's princely household as side chamber primary consort.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年，封嫻妃。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianlong, she was enfeoffed as Consort Xian.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianlong, she was made Consort Xian.

sentences.zh: 十年，進貴妃。

translations.literal: In the tenth year she was advanced to Imperial Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year she was advanced to Imperial Consort.

sentences.zh: 孝賢皇后崩，進皇貴妃，攝六宮事。

translations.literal: When Empress Xiaoxian died, she was advanced to Imperial Noble Consort and acted as mistress of the six palaces.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Xiaoxian died, she was advanced to Imperial Noble Consort and acted as mistress of the six palaces.

sentences.zh: 十五年，冊為皇后。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year she was invested as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year she was invested as empress.

sentences.zh: 三十年，從上南巡，至杭州，忤上旨，后剪髮，上益不懌，令后先還京師。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, accompanying the sovereign on a southern tour to Hangzhou, she offended the sovereign's will; the empress cut her hair; the sovereign was further displeased and ordered the empress to return first to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, accompanying the emperor on a southern tour to Hangzhou, she offended the emperor's will; the empress cut her hair; the emperor was further displeased and ordered the empress to return first to the capital.

sentences.zh: 三十一年七月甲午，崩。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, seventh month, on jiawu day, she died.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year, seventh month, on jiawu day, she died.

sentences.zh: 上方幸木蘭，命喪儀視皇貴妃。

translations.literal: The sovereign was then at Mulan; he ordered funeral rites to follow the precedent for an imperial noble consort.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then at Mulan; he ordered funeral rites to follow the precedent for an imperial noble consort.

sentences.zh: 自是遂不復立皇后。

translations.literal: From then on he never again established an empress.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he never again established an empress.

sentences.zh: 子二，永璂、永璟。

translations.literal: Sons, two: Yongji and Yongjing.
translations.idiomatic: She bore two sons: Yongji and Yongjing.

sentences.zh: 女一，殤。

translations.literal: Daughters, one: died in infancy.
translations.idiomatic: She bore one daughter, who died in infancy.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，上東巡，有金從善者，上書，首及建儲，次為立后。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year, during the eastern tour, one Jin Congshan submitted a memorial, first on establishing an heir, second on establishing an empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year, during the eastern tour, one Jin Congshan submitted a memorial, first on establishing an heir, second on establishing an empress.

sentences.zh: 上因諭曰：「那拉氏本朕青宮時皇考所賜側室福晉，孝賢皇后崩後，循序進皇貴妃。

translations.literal: The sovereign therefore issued an edict saying: "The Nara clan was originally the side chamber primary consort my Imperial Father granted me during my years in the eastern palace; after Empress Xiaoxian died, she was advanced in due order to Imperial Noble Consort.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore issued an edict saying: "The Nara clan was originally the side chamber primary consort my father granted me during my years in the eastern palace; after Empress Xiaoxian died, she was advanced in due order to Imperial Noble Consort.

sentences.zh: 越三年，立為后。

translations.literal: Three years later she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later she was established as empress.

sentences.zh: 其後自獲過愆，朕優容如故。

translations.literal: Afterward, though she had committed faults, I still treated her with the same forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, though she had committed faults, I still treated her with the same forbearance.

sentences.zh: 國俗忌剪髮，而竟悍然不顧，朕猶包含不行廢斥。

translations.literal: By national custom hair-cutting was taboo, yet she brazenly disregarded this; I still contained myself and did not depose or dismiss her.
translations.idiomatic: By national custom hair-cutting was taboo, yet she brazenly disregarded this; I still contained myself and did not depose or dismiss her.

sentences.zh: 后以病薨，止令減其儀文，並未削其位號。

translations.literal: The empress died of illness; I only ordered her funeral rites reduced and did not strip her rank or title.
translations.idiomatic: The empress died of illness; I only ordered her funeral rites reduced and did not strip her rank or title.

sentences.zh: 朕處此仁至義盡，況自是不復繼立皇后。

translations.literal: I have been benevolent to the utmost; moreover, from then on I did not again establish an empress.
translations.idiomatic: I have been benevolent to the utmost; moreover, from then on I did not again establish an empress.

sentences.zh: 從善乃欲朕下詔罪己，朕有何罪當自責乎？

translations.literal: Congshan would have me issue an edict blaming myself—what crime do I have for which to reproach myself?
translations.idiomatic: Congshan would have me issue an edict blaming myself—what crime do I have for which to reproach myself?

sentences.zh: 從善又請立后，朕春秋六十有八，豈有復冊中宮之理？」

translations.literal: Congshan also asked that an empress be established; I am sixty-eight years old—how could there be reason to invest another empress in the central palace?"
translations.idiomatic: Congshan also asked that an empress be established; I am sixty-eight years old—how could there be reason to invest another empress in the central palace?"

sentences.zh: 下行在王大臣議從善罪，坐斬。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the princes and ministers traveling with him to deliberate on Congshan's crime; he was sentenced to execution.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the princes and ministers traveling with him to deliberate on Congshan's crime; he was sentenced to execution.

sentences.zh: 孝儀純皇后，魏佳氏，內管領清泰女。

translations.literal: Empress Xiaoyi Chun, of the Weijia clan, was the daughter of Interior Manager Qingtai.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaoyi Chun, of the Weijia clan, was the daughter of Interior Manager Qingtai.

sentences.zh: 事高宗為貴人。

translations.literal: She attended Gaozong as Lady of Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: She attended Gaozong as Lady of Attendance.

sentences.zh: 封令嬪，累進令貴妃。

translations.literal: She was enfeoffed as Lady Ling and repeatedly advanced to Noble Consort Ling.
translations.idiomatic: She was made Lady Ling and repeatedly advanced to Noble Consort Ling.

sentences.zh: 年十月丁丑，仁宗生。

translations.literal: In the tenth month on dingchou day Renzong was born.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on dingchou day, Renzong was born.

sentences.zh: 三十年，進令皇貴妃。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year she was advanced to Imperial Noble Consort Ling.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year she was advanced to Imperial Noble Consort Ling.

sentences.zh: 四十年正月丁丑，薨，年四十九。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fortieth year on dingchou day she died, aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fortieth year, on dingchou day, she died, aged forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 諡曰令懿皇貴妃，葬勝水峪。

translations.literal: Her posthumous title was Imperial Noble Consort Lingyi; she was buried at Shengshui Valley.
translations.idiomatic: She was posthumously titled Imperial Noble Consort Lingyi and buried at Shengshui Valley.

sentences.zh: 六十年，仁宗立為皇太子，命冊贈孝儀皇后。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year Renzong was established as crown prince, and she was ordered posthumously invested as Empress Xiaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year Renzong was established as crown prince, and she was posthumously invested as Empress Xiaoyi.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶、道光累加諡，曰孝儀恭順康裕慈仁端恪敏哲翼天毓聖純皇后。

translations.literal: Under Jiaqing and Daoguang additional posthumous honorifics were repeatedly added, so that she was called Empress Xiaoyi Gongshun Kangyu Ciren Duanke Minzhe Yitian Yusheng Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaqing and Daoguang added further posthumous honorifics until she was styled Empress Xiaoyi Gongshun Kangyu Ciren Duanke Minzhe Yitian Yusheng Chun.

sentences.zh: 后家魏氏，本漢軍，擡入滿洲旗，改魏佳氏。

translations.literal: The empress's clan Wei was originally Han Banner; it was elevated into the Manchu Banner and changed to Weijia.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's clan Wei was originally Han Banner; it was elevated into the Manchu Banner and changed to Weijia.

sentences.zh: 子四：永璐，殤；

translations.literal: Sons, four: Yonglu, died in infancy;
translations.idiomatic: She bore four sons: Yonglu, who died in infancy;

sentences.zh: 仁宗；

translations.literal: Renzong;
translations.idiomatic: Renzong;

sentences.zh: 永璘；

translations.literal: Yonglin;
translations.idiomatic: Yonglin;

sentences.zh: 其一殤，未命名。

translations.literal: one died in infancy, unnamed.
translations.idiomatic: and one who died in infancy, unnamed.

sentences.zh: 女二，下嫁拉旺多爾濟、札蘭泰。

translations.literal: Daughters, two: married downward to Lawangduo'erji and Zhalanduo.
translations.idiomatic: She bore two daughters, who married Lawangduo'erji and Zhalanduo.

sentences.zh: 慧賢皇貴妃，高佳氏，大學士高斌女。

translations.literal: Imperial Noble Consort Huixian, of the Gaojia clan, was the daughter of Grand Secretary Gao Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Noble Consort Huixian, of the Gaojia clan, was the daughter of Grand Secretary Gao Bin.

sentences.zh: 事高宗潛邸，為側室福晉。

translations.literal: She attended Gaozong's princely household as side chamber primary consort.
translations.idiomatic: She attended Gaozong's princely household as side chamber primary consort.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，封貴妃。

translations.literal: Early in Qianlong she was enfeoffed as Imperial Consort.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianlong she was made Imperial Consort.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡曰慧賢皇貴妃。

translations.literal: She died; her posthumous title was Imperial Noble Consort Huixian.
translations.idiomatic: She died and was posthumously titled Imperial Noble Consort Huixian.

sentences.zh: 葬勝水峪。

translations.literal: She was buried at Shengshui Valley.
translations.idiomatic: She was buried at Shengshui Valley.

sentences.zh: 純惠皇貴妃，蘇佳氏。

translations.literal: Imperial Noble Consort Chunhui, of the Sujia clan.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Noble Consort Chunhui, of the Sujia clan.

sentences.zh: 事高宗潛邸。

translations.literal: She attended Gaozong's princely household.
translations.idiomatic: She attended Gaozong's princely household.

sentences.zh: 即位，封純嬪。

translations.literal: Upon his accession she was enfeoffed as Lady Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his accession she was made Lady Chun.

sentences.zh: 累進純皇貴妃。

translations.literal: She was repeatedly advanced to Imperial Noble Consort Chun.
translations.idiomatic: She was repeatedly advanced to Imperial Noble Consort Chun.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡曰純惠皇貴妃。

translations.literal: She died; her posthumous title was Imperial Noble Consort Chunhui.
translations.idiomatic: She died and was posthumously titled Imperial Noble Consort Chunhui.

sentences.zh: 葬裕陵側。

translations.literal: She was buried beside the Yu Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: She was buried beside the Yu Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 子一，永瑢。

translations.literal: Sons, one: Yongrong.
translations.idiomatic: She bore one son, Yongrong.

sentences.zh: 女一，下嫁福隆安。

translations.literal: Daughters, one: married downward to Fulong'an.
translations.idiomatic: She bore one daughter, who married Fulong'an.

sentences.zh: 慶恭皇貴妃，陸氏。

translations.literal: Imperial Noble Consort Qinggong, of the Lu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Noble Consort Qinggong, of the Lu clan.

sentences.zh: 初封慶嬪。

translations.literal: She was initially enfeoffed as Lady Qing.
translations.idiomatic: She was initially made Lady Qing.

sentences.zh: 累進慶貴妃。

translations.literal: She was repeatedly advanced to Imperial Consort Qing.
translations.idiomatic: She was repeatedly advanced to Imperial Consort Qing.

sentences.zh: 薨。

translations.literal: She died.
translations.idiomatic: She died.

sentences.zh: 仁宗以嘗受妃撫育，追尊為慶恭皇貴妃。

translations.literal: Because Renzong had once been raised by the consort, she was posthumously honored as Imperial Noble Consort Qinggong.
translations.idiomatic: Because Renzong had once been raised by her, she was posthumously honored as Imperial Noble Consort Qinggong.

sentences.zh: 哲憫皇貴妃，富察氏。

translations.literal: Imperial Noble Consort Zhemin, of the Fuca clan.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Noble Consort Zhemin, of the Fuca clan.

sentences.zh: 事高宗潛邸，

translations.literal: She attended Gaozong's princely household.
translations.idiomatic: She attended Gaozong's princely household.

sentences.zh: 雍正十三年，薨。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongzheng, she died.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Yongzheng, she died.

sentences.zh: 孝慎成皇后，佟佳氏，三等承恩公舒明阿女。

translations.literal: Empress Xiaoshen Cheng, of the Tunggiya clan, was the daughter of Shuming'a, Duke of the Third Rank of Chengen.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaoshen Cheng, of the Tunggiya clan, was the daughter of Shuming'a, Duke of the Third Rank of Chengen.

sentences.zh: 宣宗為皇子，嫡福晉薨，仁宗冊后繼嫡福晉。

translations.literal: While Xuanzong was still a prince, when the primary fujin died Renzong invested the empress to succeed as primary fujin.
translations.idiomatic: While Xuanzong was still a prince, after the primary fujin died Renzong invested her to succeed as primary fujin.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，立為皇后。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong acceded to the throne, she was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong acceded to the throne, she was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 道光十三年四月己巳，崩，諡曰孝慎皇后，葬龍泉峪。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Daoguang, fourth month on jisi day she died; her posthumous title was Empress Xiaoshen; she was buried at Longquan Valley.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Daoguang, in the fourth month, on jisi day, she died; she was posthumously titled Empress Xiaoshen and buried at Longquan Valley.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，上諡。

translations.literal: Early in Xianfeng the sovereign conferred a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianfeng reign the emperor conferred a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 光緒間加諡，曰孝慎敏肅哲順和懿誠惠敦恪熙天詒聖成皇后。

translations.literal: During the Guangxu reign additional honorifics were added, so that she was called Empress Xiaoshen Minshu Zhezhe Shunhe Yicheng Huidun Ke Xitian Yisheng Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangxu reign further honorifics were added, and she was styled Empress Xiaoshen Minshu Zhezhe Shunhe Yicheng Huidun Ke Xitian Yisheng Cheng.

sentences.zh: 女一，殤。

translations.literal: Daughters, one: died in infancy.
translations.idiomatic: She bore one daughter, who died in infancy.

sentences.zh: 孝全成皇后，鈕祜祿氏，二等侍衛、一等男頤齡女。

translations.literal: Empress Xiaoquan Cheng, of the Niohuru clan, was the daughter of Yiling, Second-Rank Bodyguard and Baron of the First Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaoquan Cheng, of the Niohuru clan, was the daughter of Yiling, Second-Rank Bodyguard and Baron of the First Rank.

sentences.zh: 后事宣宗，冊全嬪。

translations.literal: The empress attended Xuanzong and was invested as Dame Quan.
translations.idiomatic: She attended Xuanzong and was invested as Dame Quan.

sentences.zh: 累進全貴妃。

translations.literal: She was repeatedly promoted to Imperial Consort Quan.
translations.idiomatic: She was promoted in stages to Imperial Consort Quan.

sentences.zh: 道光十一年六月己丑，文宗生。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Daoguang, sixth month on jichou day Wenzong was born.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Daoguang, in the sixth month, on jichou day, Wenzong was born.

sentences.zh: 十三年，進皇貴妃，攝六宮事。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year she was promoted to Imperial Noble Consort and administered the affairs of the Six Palaces.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year she was made Imperial Noble Consort and placed in charge of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 十四年，立為皇后。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year she was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year she was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 二十年正月壬寅，崩，年三十三。

translations.literal: First month on renyin day of the twentieth year she died, aged thirty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month, on renyin day of the twentieth year, she died, aged thirty-three.

sentences.zh: 宣宗親定諡曰孝全皇后，葬龍泉峪。

translations.literal: Xuanzong personally fixed her posthumous title as Empress Xiaoquan, and she was buried at Longquan Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong personally fixed her posthumous title as Empress Xiaoquan, and she was buried at Longquan Valley.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，上諡。

translations.literal: Early in Xianfeng the sovereign conferred a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianfeng reign the emperor conferred a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 光緒間加諡，曰孝全慈敬寬仁端慤安惠誠敏符天篤聖成皇后。

translations.literal: During the Guangxu reign additional honorifics were added, so that she was called Empress Xiaoquan Cijing Kuanren Duanyin Anhui Chenmin Futian Dusheng Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangxu reign further honorifics were added, and she was styled Empress Xiaoquan Cijing Kuanren Duanyin Anhui Chenmin Futian Dusheng Cheng.

sentences.zh: 子一，文宗。

translations.literal: Sons, one: Wenzong.
translations.idiomatic: She bore one son, Wenzong.

sentences.zh: 女二：一殤，一下嫁德穆楚克扎布。

translations.literal: Daughters, two: one died in infancy; one married downward to Demuchukezhabu.
translations.idiomatic: She bore two daughters: one died in infancy; one married Demuchukezhabu.

sentences.zh: 孝靜成皇后，博爾濟吉特氏，刑部員外郎花良阿女。

translations.literal: Empress Xiaojing Cheng, of the Borjigit clan, was the daughter of Hualiang'a, Section Director of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaojing Cheng, of the Borjigit clan, was the daughter of Hualiang'a, Section Director of the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 后事宣宗為靜貴人。

translations.literal: The empress attended Xuanzong as Lady Jing of Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: She attended Xuanzong as Lady Jing of Attendance.

sentences.zh: 累進靜皇貴妃。

translations.literal: She was repeatedly promoted to Imperial Noble Consort Jing.
translations.idiomatic: She was promoted in stages to Imperial Noble Consort Jing.

sentences.zh: 孝全皇后崩，文宗方十歲，妃撫育有恩。

translations.literal: When Empress Xiaoquan died, Wenzong was just ten years old; the consort raised him with kindness.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Xiaoquan died, Wenzong was only ten; the consort raised him with devoted kindness.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，尊為皇考康慈皇貴太妃，居壽康宮。

translations.literal: When Wenzong acceded to the throne, she was honored as his father's Grand Imperial Noble Consort Kangci, and she resided in the Shoukang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong acceded to the throne, she was honored as his father's Grand Imperial Noble Consort Kangci and resided in the Shoukang Palace.

sentences.zh: 咸豐五年七月，太妃病篤，尊為康慈皇太后。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianfeng, in the seventh month, when the grand consort was gravely ill, she was honored as Empress Dowager Kangci.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xianfeng, in the seventh month, when she fell gravely ill, she was honored as Empress Dowager Kangci.

sentences.zh: 越九日庚午，崩，年四十四。

translations.literal: Nine days later on gengwu day she died, aged forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Nine days later, on gengwu day, she died, aged forty-four.

sentences.zh: 上諡，曰孝靜康慈弼天撫聖皇后，不系宣宗諡，不祔廟。

translations.literal: The sovereign conferred a posthumous title: Empress Xiaojing Kangci Bitian Fusheng; it was not linked to Xuanzong's posthumous title, and her tablet was not enshrined in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: She was posthumously titled Empress Xiaojing Kangci Bitian Fusheng; the title was not linked to Xuanzong's posthumous name, and her tablet was not enshrined in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 葬慕陵東，曰慕東陵。

translations.literal: She was buried east of the Mu Mausoleum, called the Mudong Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: She was buried east of the Mu Mausoleum, at what is called the Mudong Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，祔廟，加諡。

translations.literal: When Muzong acceded to the throne, her tablet was enshrined in the temple and additional honorifics were added.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong acceded to the throne, her tablet was enshrined in the ancestral temple and further honorifics were added.

sentences.zh: 光緒、宣統累加諡，曰孝靜康慈懿昭端惠莊仁和慎弼天撫聖成皇后。

translations.literal: Under Guangxu and Xuantong additional honorifics were repeatedly added, so that she was called Empress Xiaojing Kangci Yizhao Duanhui Zhuangren He Shen Bitian Fusheng Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Under Guangxu and Xuantong further honorifics were added until she was styled Empress Xiaojing Kangci Yizhao Duanhui Zhuangren He Shen Bitian Fusheng Cheng.

sentences.zh: 子三：奕綱、奕繼、奕訢。

translations.literal: Sons, three: Yi Gang, Yi Ji, and Yi Xin.
translations.idiomatic: She bore three sons: Yi Gang, Yi Ji, and Yi Xin.

sentences.zh: 女一，下嫁景壽。

translations.literal: Daughters, one: married downward to Jingshou.
translations.idiomatic: She bore one daughter, who married Jingshou.

sentences.zh: 莊順皇貴妃，烏雅氏。

translations.literal: Imperial Noble Consort Zhuangshun, of the Uya clan.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Noble Consort Zhuangshun, of the Uya clan.

sentences.zh: 事宣宗，為常在。

translations.literal: She attended Xuanzong as Lady of the Presence.
translations.idiomatic: She attended Xuanzong as Lady of the Presence.

sentences.zh: 進琳貴人，累進琳貴妃。

translations.literal: She was promoted to Lady Lin of Attendance and repeatedly promoted to Imperial Consort Lin.
translations.idiomatic: She was promoted to Lady Lin of Attendance and eventually to Imperial Consort Lin.

sentences.zh: 文宗尊為皇考琳貴太妃。

translations.literal: Wenzong honored her as his father's Grand Imperial Consort Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong honored her as his father's Grand Imperial Consort Lin.

sentences.zh: 穆宗尊為皇祖琳皇貴太妃。

translations.literal: Muzong honored her as his grandfather's Grand Imperial Noble Consort Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong honored her as his grandfather's Grand Imperial Noble Consort Lin.

sentences.zh: 同治五年，薨，命王公百官持服一日，諡曰莊順皇貴妃，葬慕東陵園寢。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tongzhi she died; princes, dukes, and officials were ordered to wear mourning for one day; her posthumous title was Imperial Noble Consort Zhuangshun; she was buried in the garden tomb at the Mudong Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 5 she died; princes, dukes, and officials were ordered to wear mourning for one day; she was posthumously titled Imperial Noble Consort Zhuangshun and buried in the garden tomb at the Mudong Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 德宗朝，迭命增祭品，崇規制，上親詣行禮。

translations.literal: During the Dezong reign, orders were repeatedly issued to increase sacrificial offerings and elevate ritual standards, and the sovereign personally went to perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangxu reign, orders were repeatedly issued to increase sacrificial offerings and elevate ritual standards, and the emperor personally went to perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 封三代，皆一品。

translations.literal: Three generations of her forebears were enfeoffed, all of the First Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations of her forebears were enfeoffed, all at the First Rank.

sentences.zh: 子三，奕譞、奕詥、奕譓。

translations.literal: Sons, three: Yi Huan, Yi He, and Yi Hui.
translations.idiomatic: She bore three sons: Yi Huan, Yi He, and Yi Hui.

sentences.zh: 女一，下嫁德徽。

translations.literal: Daughters, one: married downward to Dehui.
translations.idiomatic: She bore one daughter, who married Dehui.

sentences.zh: 彤貴妃，舒穆嚕氏。

translations.literal: Imperial Consort Tong, of the Sumuru clan.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Consort Tong, of the Sumuru clan.

sentences.zh: 事宣宗，為彤貴人。

translations.literal: She attended Xuanzong as Lady Tong of Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: She attended Xuanzong as Lady Tong of Attendance.

sentences.zh: 累進彤貴妃。

translations.literal: She was repeatedly promoted to Imperial Consort Tong.
translations.idiomatic: She was promoted in stages to Imperial Consort Tong.

sentences.zh: 復降貴人。

translations.literal: She was again demoted to Lady of Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: She was later demoted back to Lady of Attendance.

sentences.zh: 文宗尊為皇考彤嬪。

translations.literal: Wenzong honored her as his father's Dame Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong honored her as his father's Dame Tong.

sentences.zh: 穆宗累尊為皇祖彤貴妃。

translations.literal: Muzong repeatedly honored her as his grandfather's Imperial Consort Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong repeatedly honored her as his grandfather's Imperial Consort Tong.

sentences.zh: 女二，一下嫁扎拉豐阿，一殤。

translations.literal: Daughters, two: one married downward to Zhala Feng'a; one died in infancy.
translations.idiomatic: She bore two daughters: one married Zhala Feng'a; one died in infancy.

sentences.zh: 宣宗諸妃有子女者：*和妃，納喇氏。

translations.literal: Among Xuanzong's consorts who had children: *Consort He, of the Nara clan.
translations.idiomatic: Among Xuanzong's consorts who had children: Consort He, of the Nara clan.

sentences.zh: 初以宮女子，事宣宗潛邸，

translations.literal: Originally a palace maid, she attended Xuanzong's princely household.
translations.idiomatic: Originally a palace maid, she served in Xuanzong's princely household.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十三年，子奕緯生。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jiaqing, the son Yi Wei was born.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Jiaqing, she gave birth to the son Yi Wei.

sentences.zh: 仁宗特命為側室福晉。

translations.literal: Renzong specially ordered that she be made side chamber primary consort.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong specially ordered that she be made side chamber primary consort.

sentences.zh: 道光初，封和嬪。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daoguang she was enfeoffed as Dame He.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daoguang reign she was made Dame He.

sentences.zh: 進和妃。

translations.literal: She was promoted to Consort He.
translations.idiomatic: She was promoted to Consort He.

sentences.zh: *祥妃，鈕祜祿氏。

translations.literal: *Consort Xiang, of the Niohuru clan.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Xiang, of the Niohuru clan.

sentences.zh: 事宣宗，為貴人。

translations.literal: She attended Xuanzong as Lady of Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: She attended Xuanzong as Lady of Attendance.

sentences.zh: 進嬪，復降。

translations.literal: She was promoted to dame, then demoted again.
translations.idiomatic: She was promoted to dame, then demoted again.

sentences.zh: 文宗尊為皇考祥妃。

translations.literal: Wenzong honored her as his father's Consort Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong honored her as his father's Consort Xiang.

sentences.zh: 穆宗追尊為皇祖祥妃。

translations.literal: Muzong posthumously honored her as his grandfather's Consort Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong posthumously honored her as his grandfather's Consort Xiang.

sentences.zh: 子一，奕誴。

translations.literal: Sons, one: Yi Zai.
translations.idiomatic: She bore one son, Yi Zai.

sentences.zh: 女二，一殤，一下嫁恩醇。

translations.literal: Daughters, two: one died in infancy; one married downward to Enchun.
translations.idiomatic: She bore two daughters: one died in infancy; one married Enchun.

sentences.zh: 他無子女而受尊封者：*佳貴妃，郭佳氏；

translations.literal: Others who had no children but received honored ranks: *Imperial Consort Jia, of the Guojia clan;
translations.idiomatic: Others who had no children but received honored ranks: Imperial Consort Jia, of the Guojia clan;

sentences.zh: 成貴妃，鈕祜祿氏：皆事宣宗，為貴人，進嬪，復降。

translations.literal: Imperial Consort Cheng, of the Niohuru clan: all attended Xuanzong as Ladies of Attendance, were promoted to dame, then demoted again;
translations.idiomatic: and Imperial Consort Cheng, of the Niohuru clan: all attended Xuanzong as Ladies of Attendance, were promoted to dame, and were later demoted again;

sentences.zh: ;歷咸豐、同治二朝進封：*常妃，赫捨哩氏，以貴人進封；
